translations.literal: Xu Xuan, Ju Zhongzheng, Ceng Zhiyao, Diao Kan, Yao Xuan, Li Jianzhong, Hong Zhan, Lu Zhen, Cui Zundu, Chen Yue
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xuan, Ju Zhongzheng, Ceng Zhiyao, Diao Kan, Yao Xuan, Li Jianzhong, Hong Zhan, Lu Zhen, Cui Zundu, and Chen Yue

sentences.zh: 陳充，字若虛，益州成都人。

translations.literal: Chen Chong, styled Ruoxu, was a native of Chengdu in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Chong, courtesy name Ruoxu, came from Chengdu in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 家素豪盛，少以聲酒自娛，不樂從宦。

translations.literal: His family had long been wealthy and prominent; in youth he amused himself with music and wine and took no pleasure in pursuing office.
translations.idiomatic: Born into a wealthy house, he spent his youth on music and wine and had little taste for official life.

sentences.zh: 邑人敦迫赴舉，至京師，有名場屋間。

translations.literal: Townsmen earnestly pressed him to take the examinations; he went to the capital and won a name among those in the examination halls.
translations.idiomatic: Neighbors pressed him to sit for the examinations; once in the capital he made a name among the degree candidates.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，天府、禮部奏名皆為進士之冠，廷試擢甲科，釋褐孟州觀察推官，就改掌書記。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, his names submitted by the Directorate of Education and the Ministry of Rites both ranked first among jinshi; in the palace examination he was placed in the top class. On leaving office he was made investigating clerk in the Mengzhou observation commission, and soon after was transferred to secretary.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi (984–987) he topped both the Directorate and Ministry rosters of jinshi candidates and earned the highest palace-examination grade. On entering service he became investigating clerk on the Mengzhou observation commission, then secretary.

sentences.zh: 會寇準薦其文學，得召試，授殿中丞，出知明州。

translations.literal: When Kou Zhun recommended him for his literary learning, he was summoned for a special examination, appointed Palace Attendant, and sent out as prefect of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun's recommendation of his scholarship brought a summons to court examination, appointment as Palace Attendant, and a posting as prefect of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為太常博士、直昭文館，遷工部、刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered service as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and duty scholar in the Zhaowen Hall, and was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministries of Works and Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as Erudite of Imperial Sacrifices and Zhaowen Hall scholar, then rose to vice director in the Ministries of Works and Punishments.

sentences.zh: 久病告滿，除籍，真宗憐其貧病，令致仕，給半奉。

translations.literal: After long illness he exhausted his leave and was struck from the rolls; Emperor Zhenzong pitied his poverty and sickness, ordered him to retire, and granted half salary.
translations.idiomatic: Prolonged illness exhausted his leave and cost him his register; Zhenzong, pitying his poverty and illness, let him retire on half pay.

sentences.zh: 未幾病間，守本官，仍充職。

translations.literal: Before long his illness eased; he kept his former rank and still held his post.
translations.idiomatic: When he recovered somewhat he kept his rank and returned to duty.

sentences.zh: 以久次，遷兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: By length of service he was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Seniority brought promotion to Vice Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 景德中，與趙安仁同知貢舉，改工部、刑部郎中。

translations.literal: In the Jingde era he served with Zhao Anren as co-examiner for the metropolitan degree, and was made Director in the Ministries of Works and Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jingde (1004–1007) he and Zhao Anren jointly ran the metropolitan examinations and he became director in the Ministries of Works and Punishments.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符六年，以足疾不任朝謁，出權西京留守御史臺，旋以本官分司，卒，年七十。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dazhong xiangfu (1013), foot ailment kept him from court audience; he went out as acting commissioner of the Western Capital censorate, then served in his rank on detached duty and died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Dazhong xiangfu (1013), lameness kept him from court; he was posted acting commissioner of the Western Capital censorate, later served in his rank on detached duty, and died at seventy.

sentences.zh: 充詞學典贍，唐牛僧孺著《善惡無餘論》，言堯舜之善、伯鯀之惡，俱不能慶殃及其子，充因作論以反之，文多不載。

translations.literal: Chong's literary learning was ample and polished. Tang Niuzengru wrote 'On Good and Evil Leaving No Surplus,' arguing that the goodness of Yao and Shun and the wickedness of Gun could not bring reward or punishment upon their sons; Chong wrote a treatise to refute this, but most of the text is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: A master of polished prose, Chong answered Tang Niuzengru's 'On Good and Evil Leaving No Surplus'—which held that Yao and Shun's virtue and Gun's guilt could not visit reward or punishment on their sons—with a counter-treatise largely lost today.

sentences.zh: 性曠達，善談謔，澹於榮利，自號「中庸子」。

translations.literal: By nature he was broad-minded and easy, skilled in banter and jest, indifferent to glory and gain, and styled himself 'Master of the Mean.'
translations.idiomatic: Broad-minded and fond of wit, indifferent to rank and profit, he called himself Master of the Mean.

sentences.zh: 上頗熟其名，以疾故不登詞職。

translations.literal: The emperor knew his name well, but because of illness he never rose to a drafting post.
translations.idiomatic: The throne knew him well, yet illness kept him from a drafting appointment.

sentences.zh: 臨終自為墓誌。

translations.literal: At the end he wrote his own epitaph.
translations.idiomatic: Near death he composed his own epitaph.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collection in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 吳淑，字正儀，潤州丹陽人。

translations.literal: Wu Shu, styled Zhengyi, was a native of Danyang in Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shu, courtesy name Zhengyi, was from Danyang in Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 父文正，事吳，至太子中允。

translations.literal: His father Wenzheng served Wu and rose to Vice Director in the Crown Prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wenzheng served the Wu state and reached Vice Director in the Crown Prince's household.

sentences.zh: 好學，多自繕寫書。

translations.literal: Fond of learning, he often copied books by hand.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and copied many books himself.

sentences.zh: 淑幼俊爽，屬文敏速。

translations.literal: Shu in childhood was clever and quick, and composed with agility.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Shu was bright and quick, writing with unusual speed.

sentences.zh: 韓熙載、潘佑以文章著名江左，一見淑，深加器重。

translations.literal: Han Xizai and Pan You were famed in the lower Yangzi for their writing; at first sight of Shu they deeply esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xizai and Pan You were the celebrated writers of the lower Yangzi; both took Shu in hand at once.

sentences.zh: 自是每有滯義，難於措詞者，必命淑賦述。

translations.literal: Henceforth whenever a passage was obscure and hard to phrase, they always ordered Shu to compose it.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a knotty passage needed wording, they set Shu to draft it.

sentences.zh: 以校書郎直內史。

translations.literal: He served as collator and duty secretary in the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was collator and duty secretary in the Inner Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 江南平，歸朝，久不得調，甚窮窘。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified he submitted to the Song court and long went without appointment, in great want.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiangnan conquest he entered Song service but languished without appointment, in dire poverty.

sentences.zh: 俄以近臣延薦，試學士院，授大理評事，預修《太平御覽》、《太平廣記》、《文苑英華》。

translations.literal: Soon a close courtier recommended him; he was examined at the Hanlin Academy, appointed reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review, and took part in compiling the Taiping Imperial Reader, Taiping Extensive Records, and Forest of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: A court favorite soon secured him an Hanlin examination, appointment as judicial reviewer, and work on the Taiping Imperial Reader, Taiping Extensive Records, and Forest of Literature.

sentences.zh: 一日，召對便殿，出古碑一編，令淑與呂文仲、杜鎬讀之。

translations.literal: One day he was summoned to the side hall, where an ancient stele text was produced and he, Lü Wenzhong, and Du Gao were ordered to read it.
translations.idiomatic: One day in the side hall the emperor produced an ancient stele and had Shu, Lü Wenzhong, and Du Gao decipher it.

sentences.zh: 歷太府寺丞、著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He passed through Vice Director in the Court of the Imperial Treasury and Assistant Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice director in the Imperial Treasury and assistant compiler.

sentences.zh: 始置秘閣，以本官充校理。

translations.literal: When the Secret Archive was first established, he filled his post as collator.
translations.idiomatic: When the Secret Archive was founded he served as collator in his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 嘗獻《九弦琴五弦阮頌》，太宗賞其學問優博。

translations.literal: He once presented 'Odes on the Nine-String Zither and Five-String Lute'; Taizong praised his learning as broad and abundant.
translations.idiomatic: His 'Odes on the Nine-String Zither and Five-String Lute' won Taizong's praise for breadth of learning.

sentences.zh: 又作《事類賦》百篇以獻，詔令注釋，淑分注成三十卷上之，遷水部員外郎。

translations.literal: He also composed and presented one hundred pieces of 'Fu on Categories of Things'; the emperor ordered annotations. Shu divided the commentary into thirty juan and presented them, and was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He also presented a hundred 'Fu on Categories of Things'; ordered to annotate them, he produced thirty juan of commentary and was made Vice Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，兼掌起居舍人事，預修《太宗實錄》，再遷職方員外郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao (995) he concurrently kept the diary of attendance and helped compile the Veritable Records of Taizong, and was again promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 2 (995) he kept the attendance diary and helped compile Taizong's Veritable Records, rising again to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時諸路所上《閏年圖》，皆儀鸞司掌之，淑上言曰：「天下山川險要，皆王室之秘奧，國家之急務，故《周禮》職方氏掌天下圖籍。

translations.literal: At that time intercalary-year maps submitted from all circuits were kept by the Directorate of Palace Ceremonial. Shu memorialized: 'The perilous places of the empire's mountains and rivers are secrets of the royal house and urgent affairs of state; hence the Zhou Director of Regions kept the empire's maps and registers.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary maps from every circuit then lay with the Directorate of Palace Ceremonial. Shu argued: 'Mountain passes and rivers are royal secrets and state urgencies—the Zhou Director of Regions kept the realm's maps.

sentences.zh: 漢祖入關，蕭何收秦籍，由是周知險要，請以今閏年所納圖上職方。

translations.literal: When the Han founder entered the passes, Xiao He gathered Qin registers; thereby the perilous places were known. I ask that the maps now submitted for intercalary years be forwarded to the Directorate of Regions.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered the passes Xiao He seized Qin registers and knew every defile. Let today's intercalary maps go to the Directorate of Regions.

sentences.zh: 又州郡地裏，犬牙相入，向者獨畫一州地形，則何以傅合他郡？

translations.literal: Moreover the lands of prefectures and circuits interlock like dog's teeth; if only one circuit's terrain is drawn, how can it be fitted to the others?
translations.idiomatic: Prefecture and circuit boundaries interlock; a map of one circuit alone cannot mesh with its neighbors.

sentences.zh: 望令諸路轉運使，每十年各畫本路圖一上職方。

translations.literal: I ask that each transport commissioner every ten years submit one map of his circuit to the Directorate of Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Let every transport commissioner submit a circuit map to the Directorate every ten years.

sentences.zh: 所冀天下險要，不窺牖而可知；

translations.literal: Thus the empire's perilous places may be known without peering through a window;
translations.idiomatic: Then the realm's defiles could be known without leaving one's hall;

sentences.zh: 九州輪廣，如指掌而斯在。」

translations.literal: the breadth of the Nine Provinces would lie in the palm of the hand.'
translations.idiomatic: the Nine Provinces would lie in the palm of one's hand.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 會詔詢禦戎之策，淑抗疏請用古車戰法，上覽之，頗嘉其博學。

translations.literal: When the emperor sought strategies for border defense, Shu submitted a bold memorial urging ancient chariot warfare; on reading it the emperor greatly admired his erudition.
translations.idiomatic: Asked for frontier strategy, he urged chariot warfare of antiquity to the emperor's admiration.

sentences.zh: 咸平五年卒，年五十六。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianping (1002) he died, aged fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xianping 5 (1002), aged fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 淑性純靜好古，詞學典雅。

translations.literal: Shu by nature was pure, quiet, and fond of antiquity; his literary style was elegant and canonical.
translations.idiomatic: Pure, quiet, and devoted to antiquity, his prose was classical and refined.

sentences.zh: 初，王師圍建業，城中乏食。

translations.literal: When the imperial army first besieged Jianye, food in the city ran short.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial forces first besieged Jianye the city went hungry.

sentences.zh: 里閈有與淑同宗者，舉家皆死，惟存二女孩，淑即收養如所生，及長，嫁之。

translations.literal: In the lanes was a man of the same clan as Shu whose whole household perished, leaving only two young girls; Shu took them in and raised them as his own, and when grown gave them in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: A kinsman in his lane lost his whole household save two girls; Shu raised them as his own and married them off.

sentences.zh: 時論多其義。

translations.literal: Contemporaries widely praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Opinion widely praised his conduct.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collection in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to ten juan.

sentences.zh: 善筆劄，好篆籀，取《說文》有字義者千八百餘條，撰《說文五義》三卷。

translations.literal: Skilled with the brush, he loved seal script; taking more than eighteen hundred entries from the Shuowen with defined meanings, he compiled 'Five Meanings of the Shuowen' in three juan.
translations.idiomatic: A fine calligrapher and seal-script enthusiast, he drew eighteen hundred defined Shuowen entries into Three Juan on the Five Meanings of the Shuowen.

sentences.zh: 又著《江淮異人錄》三卷、《秘閣閑談》五卷。

translations.literal: He also wrote 'Records of Extraordinary Men of the Jiang-Huai' in three juan and 'Idle Talk of the Secret Archive' in five juan.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Records of Extraordinary Men of the Jiang-Huai (3 juan) and Idle Talk of the Secret Archive (5 juan).

sentences.zh: 子安節、讓夷、遵路皆進士及第。

translations.literal: His sons Anjie, Rangyi, and Zunlu all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Anjie, Rangyi, and Zunlu all took the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 遵路官至祠部員外郎、秘閣校理。

translations.literal: Zunlu rose to Vice Director in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and collator in the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Zunlu reached Vice Director in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Secret Archive collator.

sentences.zh: 舒雅字子正，久仕李氏。

translations.literal: Shu Ya, styled Zizheng, long served the Li house.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Ya, courtesy name Zizheng, had long served the Southern Tang Li.

sentences.zh: 江左平，為將作監丞，後充秘閣校理。

translations.literal: After the lower Yangzi was pacified he became Vice Director in the Directorate of Works, then collator in the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest he became Vice Director in the Directorate of Works, then Secret Archive collator.

sentences.zh: 好學。

translations.literal: He loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning.

sentences.zh: 善屬文，與吳淑齊名。

translations.literal: Skilled at composition, he was famed alongside Wu Shu.
translations.idiomatic: A skilled writer, he ranked with Wu Shu.

sentences.zh: 累遷職方員外郎，求出，得知舒州，仍賜金紫。

translations.literal: By repeated promotion he reached Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, sought leave, and was made prefect of Shuzhou with gold-and-purple insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, he sought a post outside and was made prefect of Shuzhou with gold-and-purple dress.

sentences.zh: 恬於榮宦，州之潛山靈仙觀有神仙勝跡，郡秩滿，即請掌觀事。

translations.literal: Indifferent to rank, he at term's end asked to take charge of the Lingxian Abbey on Mount Qian in Shuzhou, a site of immortal wonders.
translations.idiomatic: Careless of office, he at term's end took charge of the Lingxian Abbey on Shuzhou's Mount Qian, famed for immortal traces.

sentences.zh: 東封，就加主客郎中，改直昭文館，轉刑部。

translations.literal: On the eastern Fengshan rites he was added as Director in the Court of Imperial Guests, transferred to duty in the Zhaowen Hall, and moved to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern Fengshan rites brought him Director in the Court of Imperial Guests, Zhaowen duty, and transfer to Punishments.

sentences.zh: 在觀累年，優遊山水，吟詠自樂，時人美之。

translations.literal: For years in the abbey he wandered mountains and waters, composing and amusing himself, and men admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Years at the abbey among mountains and streams, composing for pleasure, won wide admiration.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十餘。

translations.literal: He died aged over seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died past seventy.

sentences.zh: 弟雄，端拱二年進士。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xiong passed the jinshi in the second year of Duangong (989).
translations.idiomatic: His brother Xiong took jinshi in Duangong 2 (989).

sentences.zh: 黃夷簡，字明舉，福州人。

translations.literal: Huang Yijian, styled Mingju, was a native of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yijian, courtesy name Mingju, was from Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父廷樞，為王審知從事，甚被親遇。

translations.literal: His father Tingchu served Wang Shenzhi as aide and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tingchu served Wang Shenzhi as aide and enjoyed great favor.

sentences.zh: 嗣王延鈞以女妻之。

translations.literal: The succeeding ruler Yanjun gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The succeeding ruler Yanjun married a daughter to him.

sentences.zh: 錢氏取福州，署光祿卿。

translations.literal: When the Qian house took Fuzhou, he was appointed Director of Imperial Entertainment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qian seized Fuzhou he was made Director of Imperial Entertainment.

sentences.zh: 夷簡少孤，好學，有名於江東，為錢惟治明州判官。

translations.literal: Yijian was orphaned young, loved learning, and was famed in the lower Yangzi; he served Qian Weizhi as judge in Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Yijian loved learning and was famed east of the river; he was Qian Weizhi's Mingzhou judge.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，隨錢俶來朝，授檢校秘書少監、元帥府掌書記，賜以襲衣、器幣、鞍勒馬。

translations.literal: In early Taiping xingguo he followed Qian Chu to court, was made Acting Vice Director of the Secretariat and secretary to the Prince of Wu's headquarters, and was given court dress, vessels, and saddled horses.
translations.idiomatic: In early Taiping xingguo he followed Qian Chu to court as Acting Vice Director of the Secretariat and headquarters secretary, with court dress, vessels, and horses.

sentences.zh: 八年，俶讓元帥，改授夷簡淮海國王府判官。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Chu yielded the prince's title and Yijian was made judge of the Prince of Huaihai's domain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Chu yielded his princely title and Yijian became judge of the Prince of Huaihai.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年，俶改封許王，出鎮南陽，加夷簡倉部員外郎，充許王府判官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi (987) Chu was enfeoffed Prince of Xu and posted to Nanyang; Yijian was added Vice Director in the Court of Revenue and made judge of the Xu prince's domain.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 4 (987) Chu became Prince of Xu at Nanyang; Yijian was made Vice Director in Revenue and judge of his domain.

sentences.zh: 初，宰相張齊賢欲引夷簡與曾致堯並知制誥，有急製，值舍人出院，即封除目命夷簡草之，物議以為不可，故但進秩而已。

translations.literal: Earlier Grand Councillor Zhang Qixian had wished to appoint Yijian with Ceng Zhiyao to draft edicts; when urgent drafts arose and the academicians were out, he would seal the appointment and order Yijian to draft. Opinion held this improper, so only rank was advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Zhang Qixian once wanted Yijian and Ceng Zhiyao as edict drafters and, when urgent drafts came with academicians absent, would seal orders for Yijian to write; opinion blocked it and he gained only rank.

sentences.zh: 景德中，夷簡被病，告滿二百日，御史臺言當除籍，真宗以其吳越舊僚，有詞學，且年老母在，特命續其月廩。

translations.literal: In Jingde Yijian fell ill; after two hundred days of leave the censorate said he should be struck from the rolls. Zhenzong, as an old Wu-Yue colleague with literary skill and an aged mother, specially continued his monthly stipend.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde illness brought two hundred days' leave and censorate demand for removal; Zhenzong, recalling a Wu-Yue colleague with learning and an aged mother, kept his stipend.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，遷秘書少監。

translations.literal: In early Dazhong xiangfu he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dazhong xiangfu he became Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三年，丁內艱，上遣中使存問，賻贈有加，因請護母喪歸浙右，許之。

translations.literal: In the third year he mourned his mother; the emperor sent envoys to inquire and added funeral gifts; he asked to escort her bier to the lower Yangzi and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he mourned his mother; the throne sent envoys with gifts and allowed him to escort her bier to the lower Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 且欲不絕其奉給，特授檢校秘書監、平江軍節度副使。

translations.literal: The emperor also wished not to cut off his salary and specially appointed him Acting Director of the Secretariat and military vice commissioner of Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Not wishing to end his pay, the throne made him Acting Director of the Secretariat and Pingjiang vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: More than a year later he died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died at seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 夷簡喜談論，善屬文，尤工詩詠，老而不輟。

translations.literal: Yijian loved talk and was skilled at composition, especially poetry, which he never ceased even in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Fond of talk and skilled in prose, especially poetry, which he never abandoned in age.

sentences.zh: 嘗攝鴻臚卿，護許國長公主葬，在道，駙馬都尉魏咸信禮接甚薄，夷簡銜之，言於上云：「發引之日，以錢三十千遺臣治裝，不重王人，若有輕國命之意，臣拒不納。」

translations.literal: Once acting Director of Imperial Banquets, he escorted the burial of Princess Chang of Xu; on the road the emperor's son-in-law Wei Xianxin treated him very coldly. Yijian bore a grudge and told the emperor: 'On the day the procession set out he gave me thirty thousand cash for travel expenses—disrespect to the imperial envoy, as if belittling the state's command. I refused.'
translations.idiomatic: Acting Director of Imperial Banquets for Princess Chang of Xu's funeral, he found the emperor's son-in-law Wei Xianxin cold on the road and told the throne: 'On departure day he offered thirty thousand cash for my outfit—slighting the imperial envoy as if the mission were light. I refused.'

sentences.zh: 上遣中使詰咸信，咸信言：「夷簡始受命，屢有求丐，又獻挽詞以希賂遺，臣皆不敢受，以是為慊。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent an envoy to question Xianxin, who said: 'When Yijian first received the order he repeatedly begged favors and presented elegies hoping for gifts; I dared accept none, hence his resentment.'
translations.idiomatic: An envoy questioned Xianxin, who said Yijian had begged favors and offered elegies for gifts he would not accept.

sentences.zh: 既而夷簡又貢歌詩一編，大率譏咸信吝嗇，且形於怨詛。

translations.literal: Then Yijian also presented a collection of songs mostly mocking Xianxin's stinginess, with resentment and curse plain.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian then presented songs mocking Xianxin's stinginess in open resentment.

sentences.zh: 復言所未受三十千錢，意欲索取。

translations.literal: He again spoke of the thirty thousand cash not received, intending to claim it.
translations.idiomatic: He still pressed the thirty thousand cash he had refused.

sentences.zh: 真宗甚鄙之，且不欲其歌詩流布於外，命中書召夷簡對焚之。

translations.literal: Zhenzong despised this and, not wanting the songs circulated, ordered the Secretariat to summon Yijian and burn them in his presence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong despised him, forbade circulation, and had the Secretariat summon him to burn the songs before him.

sentences.zh: 士大夫以是薄其為人。

translations.literal: Scholars and officials therefore held his character cheap.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen therefore thought little of his character.

sentences.zh: 浙右士之秀者，又有盧稹、謝炎、許洞。

translations.literal: Among talented men of the lower Yangzi were also Lu Zhen, Xie Yan, and Xu Dong.
translations.idiomatic: Other fine men of the lower Yangzi included Lu Zhen, Xie Yan, and Xu Dong.

sentences.zh: 盧稹字淑微，杭州人。

translations.literal: Lu Zhen, styled Shuwei, was a native of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhen, courtesy name Shuwei, was from Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼穎悟，七歲能詩，十二學屬文。

translations.literal: Clever in childhood, at seven he could write poetry and at twelve learned parallel prose.
translations.idiomatic: Clever as a child, he wrote verse at seven and parallel prose at twelve.

sentences.zh: 及長，曉《五經》大義，酷嗜《周易》、《孟子》。

translations.literal: When grown he understood the broad meaning of the Five Classics and deeply loved the Changes and Mencius.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he grasped the Five Classics and loved the Changes and Mencius.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，遊京師，時徐弦以宿儒為士子所宗，覽稹文，甚奇之，為延譽於朝。

translations.literal: In early Duangong he traveled to the capital; Xu Xuan, the senior scholar whom degree candidates revered, read Zhen's writing, marveled, and praised him at court.
translations.idiomatic: In early Duangong he went to the capital; Xu Xuan, the elder scholar students revered, marveled at his writing and praised him at court.

sentences.zh: 是年登進士第，調補真定束鹿主簿。

translations.literal: That year he passed the jinshi and was posted recorder of Zhending's Donglu county.
translations.idiomatic: That year he took jinshi and was posted recorder of Donglu in Zhending.

sentences.zh: 至府，值契丹圍城，未及赴官，卒，年二十七。

translations.literal: On reaching the prefecture the Khitan were besieging the city; before he could take office he died, aged twenty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: At the prefecture the Khitan were besieging the city; before taking office he died at twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 嘗著《五帝皇極志》、《孺子問》、《翼聖書》數十篇。

translations.literal: He had written 'Records of the Five Emperors' Imperial Pole,' 'Questions of the Child,' and 'Book to Aid the Sage' in several tens of pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He left Records of the Five Emperors' Imperial Pole, Questions of the Child, and Book to Aid the Sage in several tens of pieces.

sentences.zh: 謝炎字化南，蘇州嘉興人。

translations.literal: Xie Yan, styled Huanan, was a native of Jiaxing in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yan, courtesy name Huanan, was from Jiaxing in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 父崇禮，泰寧軍掌書記。

translations.literal: His father Chongli was secretary to the Taining army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chongli was secretary to the Taining army.

sentences.zh: 炎慕韓、柳為文，與盧稹齊名，時謂之「盧、謝」。

translations.literal: Yan admired Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan in writing and was famed with Lu Zhen; contemporaries called them 'Lu and Xie.'
translations.idiomatic: Yan took Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan as models and was paired with Lu Zhen as 'Lu and Xie.'

sentences.zh: 稹忄巽懦，炎勁急，反相厚善。

translations.literal: Zhen was timid and retiring, Yan sharp and impatient, yet the two were warmly devoted to each other.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhen was timid, Xie Yan impetuous, yet they were deeply devoted friends.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，舉進士，調補昭應主簿，徙伊闕，連知華容、公安二縣，卒，年三十四。

translations.literal: In early Duangong he passed the jinshi, was posted recorder of Zhaoying, transferred to Yique, and in succession was magistrate of Huarong and Gong'an counties; he died aged thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In early Duangong he took jinshi, served as Zhaoying recorder, moved to Yique, and successively governed Huarong and Gong'an; he died at thirty-four.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collection in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 許洞字洞天，蘇州吳縣人。

translations.literal: Xu Dong, styled Dongtian, was a native of Wu county in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Dong, courtesy name Dongtian, was from Wu county in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 父仲容，太子洗馬致仕。

translations.literal: His father Zhongrong retired as Director of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongrong had retired as Director of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 洞性疏雋，幼時習弓矢擊刺之伎，及長，折節勵學，尤精《左氏傳》。

translations.literal: Dong by nature was free and sharp; in youth he practiced bow, arrow, and thrusting arts, but when grown he reformed himself and urged on his studies, especially mastering the Zuo Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Free-spirited and sharp, he trained in archery and swordplay as a boy, then turned to books and mastered the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年進士，解褐雄武軍推官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping (1000) he passed the jinshi and on leaving office was made investigating clerk in the Xiongwu army.
translations.idiomatic: He took jinshi in Xianping 3 (1000) and became investigating clerk in the Xiongwu army.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣府白事，有卒踞坐不起，即杖之。

translations.literal: Once when he went to the prefecture to report business, a soldier sat sprawled and would not rise; Dong at once beat him with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: Reporting to the prefecture once, he found a soldier sprawled and refusing to rise and caned him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 時馬知節知州，洞又移書責知節，知節怒其狂狷不遜，會洞輒用公錢，奏除名。

translations.literal: At the time Ma Zhijie was prefect; Dong also sent a letter rebuking Zhijie. Zhijie was angry at his wild insolence, and when Dong repeatedly used public funds, memorialized to strike his name from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Ma Zhijie took offense at Dong's insolent letter; when Dong misused public funds Zhijie had him removed from office.

sentences.zh: 歸吳中數年，日以酣飲為事。

translations.literal: After several years back in Wu he made heavy drinking his daily business.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Wu for years he lived for drink.

sentences.zh: 嘗從民坊貰酒，一日，大署壁作《酒歌》數百言，鄉人爭往觀，其酤數倍，乃盡捐洞所負。

translations.literal: Once he bought wine on credit from a neighborhood shop; one day he wrote several hundred words of 'Song of Wine' in large characters on the wall, and townspeople flocked to see; sales multiplied several times over, and the shopkeeper forgave all Dong owed.
translations.idiomatic: Buying wine on credit once, he covered a shop wall with a long 'Song of Wine'; crowds came, sales soared, and the shopkeeper canceled his debt.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，獻所撰《虎鈐經》二十卷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde (1005) he presented his 'Tiger Tally Classic' in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 2 (1005) he presented his Tiger Tally Classic in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 應洞識韜略、運籌決勝科，以負譴報罷，就除均州參軍。

translations.literal: He answered the examination category for mastery of strategy and planning victory, but because of the prior dismissal was rejected and only made aide in Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sat for the strategy examination but the earlier dismissal blocked promotion; he received only a Junzhou aide post.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符四年，祀汾陰，獻《三盛禮賦》，召試中書，改烏江縣主簿，卒，年四十二。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dazhong xiangfu (1011), at the Fenyin sacrifice he presented 'Fu on the Three Grand Rites,' was summoned for examination at the Secretariat, and was changed to recorder of Wuhe county; he died aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: At the Fenyin rites in Dazhong xiangfu 4 (1011) he presented his Fu on the Three Grand Rites, passed a Secretariat examination, became Wuhe recorder, and died at forty-two.

sentences.zh: 有集一百卷。

translations.literal: He left a collection in one hundred juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to one hundred juan.

sentences.zh: 又著《春秋釋幽》五卷、《演玄》十卷。

translations.literal: He also wrote 'Elucidating the Obscure in the Spring and Autumn' in five juan and 'Expounding the Mysterious' in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Elucidating the Obscure in the Spring and Autumn (5 juan) and Expounding the Mysterious (10 juan).

sentences.zh: 徐鉉，字鼎臣，揚州廣陵人。

translations.literal: Xu Xuan, styled Dingchen, was a native of Guangling in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xuan, courtesy name Dingchen, was from Guangling in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十歲能屬文，不妄遊處，與韓熙載齊名，江東謂之「韓、徐」。

translations.literal: At ten he could compose; he did not roam idly and was famed with Han Xizai; the lower Yangzi called them 'Han and Xu.'
translations.idiomatic: Composing at ten, avoiding idle wandering, he was paired with Han Xizai as Han and Xu in the lower Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 仕吳為校書郎，又仕南唐李父子，試知制誥，與宰相宋齊丘不協。

translations.literal: He served Wu as collator, then the Southern Tang Li father and son, was tried as edict drafter, and was at odds with Grand Councillor Song Qiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He collated for Wu, drafted for the Southern Tang Li, and clashed with Grand Councillor Song Qiqiu.

sentences.zh: 時有得軍中書檄者，鉉及弟鍇評其援引不當。

translations.literal: Once a military proclamation from headquarters was obtained; Xuan and his younger brother Kai judged its citations improper.
translations.idiomatic: When a military proclamation surfaced, Xuan and his brother Kai found its citations faulty.

sentences.zh: 檄乃湯悅所作，悅與齊丘誣鉉、鍇泄機事，鉉坐貶泰州司戶掾，鍇貶為烏江尉，俄復舊官。

translations.literal: The proclamation had been written by Tang Yue; Yue with Qiqiu slandered Xuan and Kai for leaking secrets. Xuan was demoted to registrar in Taizhou, Kai to magistrate of Wuhe, and soon both were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Yue had written it; he and Qiqiu accused the brothers of leaking secrets. Xuan became Taizhou registrar and Kai Wuhe magistrate, then both were restored.

sentences.zh: 時景命內臣車延規、傅宏營屯田於常、楚州，處事苛細，人不堪命，致盜賊群起。

translations.literal: At the time the inner attendant Che Yanwei and Fu Hongying managed garrison fields in Chang and Chuzhou with harsh petty measures; men could not bear it and bandits rose in groups.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants Che Yanwei and Fu Hongying ran harsh garrison fields in Chang and Chu until bandits rose in bands.

sentences.zh: 命鉉乘傳巡撫。

translations.literal: Xuan was ordered to travel on imperial commission to inspect and pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was sent on commission to inspect and pacify.

sentences.zh: 鉉至楚州，奏罷屯田，延規等懼，逃罪，鉉捕之急，權近側目。

translations.literal: At Chuzhou he memorialized to abolish the garrison fields; Yanwei and the others feared punishment and fled; Xuan pursued them hotly, and the powerful looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: At Chu he abolished the garrison fields; Yanwei fled and Xuan hunted them hard, drawing hostile glances from the powerful.

sentences.zh: 及捕得賊首，即斬之不俟報，坐專殺流舒州。

translations.literal: When he captured the bandit chief he beheaded him without awaiting report and was exiled to Shuzhou for unauthorized execution.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded a captured bandit chief without awaiting orders and was exiled to Shuzhou for unauthorized killing.

sentences.zh: 周世宗南征，景徙鉉饒州，俄召為太子右諭德，復知制誥，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Shizong campaigned south, Jing moved Xuan to Raozhou, then soon summoned him as Right Mentor to the Crown Prince, restored him as edict drafter, and promoted him to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong's southern campaign sent him to Raozhou, then recalled him as crown-prince mentor, drafter, and Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 景死，事其子煜為禮部侍郎，通署中書省事，曆尚書在丞、兵部侍郎、翰林學士、御史大夫、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Jing died, he served the son Yu as Vice Minister of Rites, concurrently handling Secretariat affairs, and passed through Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, Vice Minister of War, Hanlin academician, Censor-in-Chief, and Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing's death he served Yu as Vice Minister of Rites with Secretariat duties, rising to Left Vice Director, Vice Minister of War, Hanlin academician, Censor-in-Chief, and Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 宋師圍金陵，煜遣鉉求緩兵。

translations.literal: When Song forces besieged Jinling, Yu sent Xuan to seek a truce.
translations.idiomatic: When Song besieged Jinling Yu sent Xuan to beg a truce.

sentences.zh: 時煜將朱令贇將兵十餘萬自上江來援，煜以鉉既行，欲止令贇勿令東下。

translations.literal: At the time Yu's general Zhu Lingyun was bringing more than a hundred thousand troops down the upper Yangzi as relief; because Xuan had already set out, Yu wished to stop Lingyun from marching east.
translations.idiomatic: General Zhu Lingyun was bringing a hundred thousand men downriver; with Xuan already gone Yu wanted to halt him.

sentences.zh: 鉉曰：「此行未保必能濟難，江南所恃者援兵爾，奈何止之！」

translations.literal: Xuan said: 'This journey cannot be sure to relieve the crisis; what Jiangnan relies on is relief troops—how can you stop them!'
translations.idiomatic: Xuan said: 'This mission may not save us, but Jiangnan lives on relief troops—how can you stop them?'

sentences.zh: 煜曰：「方求和解而復決戰，豈利於汝乎？」

translations.literal: Yu said: 'You seek peace and yet battle is renewed—how does that profit you?'
translations.idiomatic: Yu said: 'You sue for peace while battle resumes—how does that help you?'

sentences.zh: 鉉曰「要以社稷為計，豈顧一介之使，置之度外可也。」

translations.literal: Xuan said: 'One must take the altars as the measure; how can one care for a single envoy? Set that aside.'
translations.idiomatic: Xuan said: 'The altars come first; a single envoy does not matter—set me aside.'

sentences.zh: 煜泣而遣之。

translations.literal: Yu wept and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Yu wept and sent him on.

sentences.zh: 及至，雖不能緩兵，而入見辭歸，禮遇皆與常時同。

translations.literal: When he arrived, though he could not slow the army, on taking leave to return he was treated with the same courtesy as before.
translations.idiomatic: He could not slow the Song army, but on leave to return he received the same courtesy as before.

sentences.zh: 及隨煜入覲，太祖責之，聲甚厲。

translations.literal: When he followed Yu to audience, Taizu rebuked him in a very stern voice.
translations.idiomatic: Entering court with Yu, he met Taizu's fierce rebuke.

sentences.zh: 鉉對曰：「臣為江南大臣，國亡罪當死，不當問其他。」

translations.literal: Xuan replied: 'Your servant was a great minister of Jiangnan; when the state perished guilt deserved death—one should not ask anything else.'
translations.idiomatic: Xuan answered: 'I was Jiangnan's minister; when the state fell I deserved death and nothing more should be asked.'

sentences.zh: 太祖歎曰：「忠臣也！

translations.literal: Taizu sighed and said: 'A loyal minister!
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sighed: 'A loyal minister!

sentences.zh: 事我當如李氏。」

translations.literal: Serve me as you served the Li house.'
translations.idiomatic: Serve me as you served the Li.'

sentences.zh: 命為太子率更令。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，李昉獨直翰林，鉉直學士院。

translations.literal: In early Taiping xingguo Li Fang alone held Hanlin duty and Xuan the academy.
translations.idiomatic: In early Taiping xingguo Li Fang held Hanlin duty alone and Xuan the academy.

sentences.zh: 從征太原，軍中書詔填委，鉉援筆無滯，辭理精當，時論能之。

translations.literal: On the Taiyuan campaign proclamations piled up in camp; Xuan wrote without delay, his reasoning precise, and contemporaries praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: On the Taiyuan campaign he drafted proclamations without delay to general praise.

sentences.zh: 師還，加給事中。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was added Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was made Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 八年，出為右散騎常侍，遷左常侍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he went out as Right Regular Attendant and was moved to Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became Right then Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，廬州女僧道安誣鉉奸私事，道安坐不實抵罪，鉉亦貶靜難行軍司馬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua (991) the nun Dao'an of Luzhou falsely accused Xuan of illicit relations; Dao'an was punished for the false charge and Xuan was demoted to staff officer on the Jingnan campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 2 (991) a Luzhou nun falsely accused him of impropriety; she was punished and he was demoted to Jingnan staff officer.

sentences.zh: 初，鉉至京師，見被毛褐者輒哂之，邠州苦寒，終不禦毛褐，致冷疾。

translations.literal: When Xuan first reached the capital he laughed at those in fur coats; Binzhou was bitterly cold yet he never wore fur and contracted a cold ailment.
translations.idiomatic: New to the capital he mocked fur coats; in bitter Binzhou he refused them and fell ill of cold.

sentences.zh: 一日晨起方冠帶，遽索筆手疏，約束後事，又別署曰：「道者，天地之母。」

translations.literal: One morning as he was dressing he suddenly asked for brush and wrote a hand memorial settling his affairs, and separately wrote: 'The Way is the mother of Heaven and Earth.'
translations.idiomatic: Dressing one morning he suddenly wrote his last affairs and added: 'The Way is the mother of Heaven and Earth.'

sentences.zh: 書訖而卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: When the writing was finished he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died as he finished, at seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 鉉無子，門人鄭文寶護其喪至汴，胡仲容歸其葬於南昌之西山。

translations.literal: Xuan had no son; his student Zheng Wenbao escorted the bier to Bian and Hu Zhongrong buried him on West Mountain at Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, his student Zheng Wenbao escorted the bier to Bian and Hu Zhongrong buried him on Nanchang's West Mountain.

sentences.zh: 鉉性簡淡寡欲，質直無矯飾，不喜釋氏而好神怪，有以此獻者，所求必如其請。

translations.literal: Xuan was plain and sparing of desire, honest without affectation, disliked Buddhism but loved the uncanny; when such things were offered what he sought was always granted.
translations.idiomatic: Plain, few in wants, honest and unadorned, he disliked Buddhism but loved marvels and always received what he asked.

sentences.zh: 鉉精小學，好李斯小篆，臻其妙，隸書亦工。

translations.literal: Xuan was expert in philology, loved Li Si's small seal script and reached its subtlety; his clerical script was also skilled.
translations.idiomatic: A philologist, he mastered Li Si's small seal and wrote fine clerical script.

sentences.zh: 嘗受詔與句中正、葛湍、王惟恭等同校《說文》，《序》曰：

translations.literal: He once received orders with Ju Zhongzheng, Ge Tuan, Wang Weigong, and others jointly to collate the Shuowen, and wrote in the preface:
translations.idiomatic: Ordered with Ju Zhongzheng and others to collate the Shuowen, he wrote in the preface:

sentences.zh: 許慎《說文》十四篇，並《序目》一篇，凡萬六百餘字，聖人之旨蓋雲備矣。

translations.literal: Xu Shen's Shuowen in fourteen chapters with one chapter of preface, in all a little more than ten thousand six hundred characters—the sage's intent is surely complete.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shen's Shuowen: fourteen chapters plus preface, over ten thousand six hundred characters—the sage's intent stands complete.

sentences.zh: 夫八卦既畫，萬象既分，則文字為之大輅，載籍為之六轡，先王教化所以行於百代，及物之功與造化均不可忽也。

translations.literal: When the Eight Trigrams were drawn and the myriad forms divided, writing became the great carriage and records the six reins; the former kings' teaching could run through a hundred generations, and its merit in reaching things equaled creation— it cannot be neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Once the trigrams were drawn and forms divided, writing became the great carriage and records the six reins; royal teaching ran through ages and its reach matched creation itself.

sentences.zh: 雖王帝之後改易殊體，六國之世文字異形，然猶存篆籀之跡，不失形類之本。

translations.literal: Though after the sage-emperors scripts changed in many forms and in the Six States characters differed in shape, still the traces of seal script remained and the root of form-classes was not lost.
translations.idiomatic: Though scripts changed under later kings and Six States forms diverged, seal traces remained and the roots of form survived.

sentences.zh: 及暴秦苛政，散隸聿興，便於末俗，人競師法。

translations.literal: When brutal Qin imposed harsh rule, clerical script suddenly arose, convenient for vulgar ends, and men vied to take it as model.
translations.idiomatic: Under brutal Qin clerical script arose for vulgar convenience and all rushed to imitate it.

sentences.zh: 古文既變，巧偽日滋。

translations.literal: The ancient script having changed, artifice and falsehood daily increased.
translations.idiomatic: With ancient script altered, artifice multiplied daily.

sentences.zh: 至漢宣帝時，始命諸儒修倉頡之法，亦不能復。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xuan's time the court first ordered the ru to restore Cangjie's method, yet still could not recover it.
translations.idiomatic: Even Xuan's order to restore Cangjie's method could not bring it back.

sentences.zh: 至光武時，馬援上疏論文字之訛謬，其言詳矣。

translations.literal: In Emperor Guangwu's time Ma Yuan memorialized on errors in writing in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu's reign brought Ma Yuan's detailed memorial on written errors.

sentences.zh: 及和帝時，申命賈逵修理舊文，於是許慎采史籀、李斯、揚雄之書，博訪通人，考之於逵，作《說文解字》，至安帝十五年始奏上之。

translations.literal: In Emperor He's time he again ordered Jia Kui to repair the old text; Xu Shen gathered the books of Shizhou, Li Si, and Yang Xiong, broadly consulted experts, checked with Kui, and composed Explaining Graphs and Analyzing Characters, presenting it in the fifteenth year of Emperor An.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Jia Kui to repair old text; Shen gathered Shizhou, Li Si, and Yang Xiong, consulted widely, checked with Kui, and composed Explaining Graphs, presenting it in An's fifteenth year.

sentences.zh: 而隸書之行已久，加以行、草、八分紛然間出，反以篆籀為奇怪之跡，不復輕心。

translations.literal: But clerical script had long been current, and running, cursive, and eight-part forms appeared in confusion, so seal script became a strange trace and men no longer took it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Clerical script already ruled; running, cursive, and eight-part forms crowded in and seal script seemed merely quaint.

sentences.zh: 至於六籍舊文，相承傳寫，多求便俗，漸失本原。

translations.literal: As for the old texts of the six classics, handed down in copy after copy, men mostly sought vulgar convenience and gradually lost the original.
translations.idiomatic: Classical texts copied on and on sought vulgar ease and lost the source.

sentences.zh: 《爾雅》所載草、木、魚、鳥之名，肆誌增益，不可觀矣。

translations.literal: The names of plants, trees, fish, and birds recorded in the Erya were recklessly increased and cannot be viewed whole.
translations.idiomatic: Erya entries for plants, fish, and birds swelled beyond recognition.

sentences.zh: 諸儒傳釋，亦非精究小學之徒，莫能矯正。

translations.literal: The exegeses of the ru were not finely studied either; none but masters of philology could correct them.
translations.idiomatic: Ru commentary was shallow; only philologists could set it right.

sentences.zh: 唐大曆中，李陽冰篆跡殊絕，獨冠古今，於是刊定《說文》，修正筆法，學者師慕，篆籀中興。

translations.literal: In the Dali era of Tang, Li Yangbing's seal traces were uniquely supreme, ancient and modern; he then revised the Shuowen and corrected brush method, and scholars admired him so seal script revived.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang's Dali era Li Yangbing's seal surpassed all ages; revising the Shuowen he revived seal script for admiring scholars.

sentences.zh: 然頗排斥許氏，自為臆說。

translations.literal: Yet he largely rejected Xu and followed his own surmise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he largely rejected Xu for private invention.

sentences.zh: 夫以師心之獨見，破先儒之祖述，豈聖人之意乎？

translations.literal: To break the forefathers' transmission by teacher's private view—can that be the sage's intent?
translations.idiomatic: To overturn the ancients on private conviction—was that the sage's intent?

sentences.zh: 今之為字學者，亦多陽冰之新義，所謂貴耳而賤目也。

translations.literal: Today's students of writing mostly follow Yangbing's new meanings—what is called honoring the ear and despising the eye.
translations.idiomatic: Today's graphologists prize Yangbing's novelties—honoring hearsay over sight.

sentences.zh: 自唐末喪亂，經籍道息。

translations.literal: From the late Tang came chaos and the way of classics ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Late Tang chaos stilled the way of classics.

sentences.zh: 有宋膺運，人文國典，粲然復興，以為文字者六藝之本，當由古法，乃詔取許慎《說文解字》，精加詳校，垂憲百代。

translations.literal: Song received the mandate; human culture and state canons flourished again. They held writing the root of the six arts and that ancient method should be followed, and ordered Xu Shen's Explaining Graphs finely collated as law for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Song revived culture, took writing as root of the six arts, and ordered a fine collation of Xu Shen's Explaining Graphs as law for ages.

sentences.zh: 臣等敢竭愚陋，備加詳考。

translations.literal: We your servants dare exhaust our foolishness and add detailed examination.
translations.idiomatic: We dare offer our shallow labors in detailed review.

sentences.zh: 有許慎注義、序例中所載而諸部不見者，審知漏落，悉從補錄。

translations.literal: Where Xu Shen's glosses or the preface list entries not found in the sections, knowing they had fallen out, we restored them all.
translations.idiomatic: Missing entries from Xu's glosses or preface we restored wherever found.

sentences.zh: 復有經典相承傳，寫及時俗要用而《說文》不載者，皆附益之，以廣篆籀之路。

translations.literal: Also canonical transmissions and current vulgar usage not in the Shuowen we added to broaden the path of seal script.
translations.idiomatic: Current usage and transmission absent from the Shuowen we added when form and sound followed the six scripts.

sentences.zh: 亦皆形聲相從、不違六書之義者。

translations.literal: All followed form and sound and did not violate the six scripts.
translations.idiomatic: All followed form and sound without violating the six scripts.

sentences.zh: 其間《說文》具有正體而時俗論變者，則具於注中。

translations.literal: Where the Shuowen had the correct form but vulgar usage had changed, we noted it in the commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Where correct Shuowen forms had vulgar variants we noted them in commentary.

sentences.zh: 其有義理乘舛、違戾六書者，並列序於後，俾夫學者無或致疑。

translations.literal: Where meaning strayed and violated the six scripts we listed them afterward so scholars would not doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Errant meanings violating the six scripts we listed after so scholars would not doubt.

sentences.zh: 大抵此書務援古以正今，不徇今而違古。

translations.literal: In general this book uses antiquity to correct the present and does not follow the present against antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: This book uses antiquity to correct the present, never the present against antiquity.

sentences.zh: 若乃高文大冊，則宜以篆籀著之金石，至於常行簡牘，則草隸足矣。

translations.literal: For lofty texts and great volumes seal script should be set in metal and stone; for ordinary documents clerical script suffices.
translations.idiomatic: Grand works belong in seal on metal and stone; daily documents need only clerical script.

sentences.zh: 又許慎注解，詞簡義奧，不可周知。

translations.literal: Xu Shen's glosses are brief in wording and deep in meaning and cannot be fully known at once.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's glosses are terse and deep beyond quick mastery.

sentences.zh: 陽冰之後，諸儒箋述有可取者，亦從附益；

translations.literal: After Yangbing, ru commentaries with merit we also added;
translations.idiomatic: Worthy ru glosses after Yangbing we also added;

sentences.zh: 猶有未盡，則臣等粗為訓釋，以成一家之書。

translations.literal: where still incomplete, we your servants roughly glossed to complete a school of the book.
translations.idiomatic: where still lacking we roughly glossed to complete one school of the book.

sentences.zh: 《說文》之時，未有反切，後人附益，互有異同。

translations.literal: In Xu Shen's time there was no fanqie; later additions differ among men.
translations.idiomatic: In Shen's day there was no fanqie; later additions disagree.

sentences.zh: 孫愐《唐韻》行之已久，今並以孫愐音切為定，庶幾學者有所適從焉。

translations.literal: Sun Mian's Tangyun has long been current; we now fix all readings by Sun Mian's fanqie so scholars may have a standard.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Mian's Tangyun now fixes all readings so scholars have a standard.

sentences.zh: 鍇亦善小學，嘗以許慎《說文》依四聲譜次為十卷，目曰《說文解字韻譜》。

translations.literal: Kai was also skilled in philology; he once arranged Xu Shen's Shuowen by the four tones into ten juan titled Rhyme Companion to Explaining Graphs.
translations.idiomatic: Kai too mastered philology and arranged the Shuowen by four tones in ten juan as Rhyme Companion to Explaining Graphs.

sentences.zh: 鉉序之曰：

translations.literal: Xuan prefaced it, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xuan prefaced it thus:

sentences.zh: 昔伏羲畫八卦而文字之端見矣，蒼頡模鳥跡而文字之形立矣。

translations.literal: Of old Fuxi drew the Eight Trigrams and the beginning of writing appeared; Cangjie modeled bird tracks and the forms of writing were established.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxi drew the trigrams and writing began; Cangjie traced bird tracks and character forms stood firm.

sentences.zh: 史籀作大篆以潤色之，李斯變小篆以簡易之，其美至矣。

translations.literal: Shizhou made great seal to adorn it, Li Si changed to small seal to simplify it—the beauty reached its height.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhou's great seal adorned it, Li Si's small seal simplified it—beauty peaked there.

sentences.zh: 及程邈作隸而人競趣省，古法一變，字義浸訛。

translations.literal: When Cheng Miao made clerical script men all rushed to abbreviate; ancient method changed once and character meaning gradually erred.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Miao's clerical script made all rush to abbreviate; ancient method shifted and meaning eroded.

sentences.zh: 先儒許慎患其若此，故集《倉》、《雅》之學，研六書之旨，博訪通識，考於賈逵，作《說文解字》十五篇，凡萬六百字。

translations.literal: The former ru Xu Shen feared this; he gathered the learning of Cangjie and Erya, studied the six scripts, broadly consulted experts, checked with Jia Kui, and composed Explaining Graphs in fifteen chapters, ten thousand six hundred characters in all.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shen gathered Cangjie and Erya, studied the six scripts, consulted Jia Kui, and wrote Explaining Graphs in fifteen chapters and ten thousand six hundred characters.

sentences.zh: 字書精博，莫過於是。

translations.literal: No character book is more refined and abundant.
translations.idiomatic: No character book surpasses it.

sentences.zh: 篆籀之體，極於斯焉。

translations.literal: Seal script reached its extreme there.
translations.idiomatic: Seal script peaked there.

sentences.zh: 其後賈魴以《三蒼》之書皆為隸字，隸字始廣而篆籀轉微。

translations.literal: Later Jia Fang took the three Cang books all as clerical characters; clerical spread and seal script waned.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jia Fang treated the three Cang as clerical; clerical spread and seal faded.

sentences.zh: 後漢及今千有餘歲，凡善書者皆草隸焉。

translations.literal: From Later Han to today more than a thousand years—every skilled writer writes clerical.
translations.idiomatic: For a thousand years since Later Han every good writer has used clerical.

sentences.zh: 又隸書之法有冊繁補闕之論，則其訛偽斷可知矣。

translations.literal: Clerical method has theories of omitting the complex and supplying the deficient—its errors and falsehoods can be known for certain.
translations.idiomatic: Clerical rules of omitting and supplying guarantee corruption.

sentences.zh: 故今字書之數累倍於前。

translations.literal: Hence the number of character books today is many times the former.
translations.idiomatic: Today's character books multiply the old count.

sentences.zh: 夫聖人創製皆有依據，不知而作，君子慎之，及史闕文，格言斯在。

translations.literal: The sage's creations all have basis; to act without knowing is what the noble man dreads—and when the Historian lacks text, that maxim stands.
translations.idiomatic: Sage creation rests on precedent; ignorant invention the noble dreads—and when records fail, that maxim stands.

sentences.zh: 若草、木、魚、鳥，形聲相從，觸類長之，良無窮極，苟不折之以古義，何足以觀？

translations.literal: Plants, trees, fish, and birds follow form and sound and grow by category without end; if not checked by ancient meaning, how can one view them?
translations.idiomatic: Plants and fish grow by form and sound without end; without ancient meaning how can one judge?

sentences.zh: 故叔重之後，《玉篇》、《切韻》所載，習俗雖久，要不可施之於篆文。

translations.literal: After Shen, what the Yupian and Qieyun record, though long customary, cannot be applied to seal text.
translations.idiomatic: After Shen, Yupian and Qieyun usages, however old, cannot govern seal.

sentences.zh: 往者，李陽冰天縱其能，中興斯學。

translations.literal: Formerly Li Yangbing by heaven's gift revived this learning.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yangbing once revived the art by heaven's gift.

sentences.zh: 讚明許氏，奐焉英發。

translations.literal: Praising Xu, he flourished brilliantly.
translations.idiomatic: Praising Xu he shone brilliantly.

sentences.zh: 然古法背俗，易為堙微。

translations.literal: Yet ancient method opposed vulgar usage and was easily buried.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ancient method opposed the vulgar and was easily lost.

sentences.zh: 方今許、李之書僅存於世，學者殊寡，舊章罕存。

translations.literal: Today the books of Xu and Li barely survive; scholars are very few and old statutes rarely remain.
translations.idiomatic: Today Xu and Li survive only in fragments; few study them and old rules are rare.

sentences.zh: 秉筆操觚，要資檢閱，而偏傍奧密，不可意知，尋求一字，往往終卷，力省功倍，思得其宜。

translations.literal: Wielding brush and tablet requires checking, yet radicals are deep and secret and cannot be known by guess; seeking one character often runs through the whole scroll—saving labor and doubling effect, one thinks to get it right.
translations.idiomatic: Brush in hand one must consult references, yet radicals are abstruse; hunting one graph can mean reading the whole scroll—hence the need for a tool that saves labor.

sentences.zh: 舍弟鍇特善小學，因命取叔重所記，以《切韻》次之，聲韻區分，開卷可睹。

translations.literal: My younger brother Kai is especially skilled in philology; I therefore ordered him to take what Uncle Shen recorded and arrange it by the Qieyun so tones and rhymes are divided and visible on opening the book.
translations.idiomatic: My brother Kai, expert in philology, arranged Shen's record by the Qieyun so tones and rhymes appear at a glance.

sentences.zh: 鍇又集《通釋》四十篇，考先賢之微言，暢許氏之玄旨，正陽冰之新義，折流俗之異端，文字之學，善矣盡矣。

translations.literal: Kai also compiled forty chapters of Comprehensive Gloss, examining the subtle words of former sages, unfolding Xu's deep intent, correcting Yangbing's new meanings, and refuting vulgar divergences—the study of writing, good and complete.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's forty chapters of Comprehensive Gloss expound the sages, unfold Xu's intent, correct Yangbing, and refute vulgar error—writing study perfected.

sentences.zh: 今此書止欲便於檢討，無恤其他，故聊存詁訓，以為別識。

translations.literal: This book now only wishes to ease consultation and cares for nothing else; hence we briefly keep glosses as a separate guide.
translations.idiomatic: This book serves lookup only; we keep brief glosses as a separate guide.

sentences.zh: 其餘敷演，有《通釋五音》凡十卷，貽諸同志雲。

translations.literal: Further exposition has Comprehensive Gloss of the Five Sounds in ten juan, left to like-minded friends.
translations.idiomatic: Further work appears in Comprehensive Gloss of the Five Sounds in ten juan for fellow scholars.

sentences.zh: 鉉親為之篆，鏤板以行於世。

translations.literal: Xuan personally wrote it in seal script and cut blocks to circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan wrote it in seal script himself and had it carved for circulation.

sentences.zh: 鍇字楚金，四歲而孤，母方教鉉，未暇及鍇，能自知書。

translations.literal: Kai, styled Chujin, was orphaned at four; his mother was teaching Xuan and had no time for Kai, yet he learned writing on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Kai, courtesy name Chujin, was orphaned at four; his mother taught Xuan and Kai taught himself to write.

sentences.zh: 李景見其文，以為秘書省正字，累官內史舍人，因鉉奉使入宋，憂懼而卒，年五十五。

translations.literal: Li Jing saw his writing and made him Rectifier in the Secretariat, rising to Inner Secretariat Drafter; when Xuan went on mission to Song he died of worry and fear, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing made him Secretariat rectifier and Inner Drafter; he died of grief when Xuan went to Song, aged fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 李穆使江南，見其兄弟文章，歎曰：「二陸不能及也！」

translations.literal: Li Mu on mission to Jiangnan saw the brothers' writing and sighed: 'The two Lu could not match them!'
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu on mission to Jiangnan sighed that the two Lu could not equal them.

sentences.zh: 鉉有文集三十卷，《質疑論》若干卷。

translations.literal: Xuan had a collected works in thirty juan and Doubting Discussions in several juan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan left thirty juan of collected works and Doubting Discussions.

sentences.zh: 所著《稽神錄》，多出於其客蒯亮。

translations.literal: His Records of Investigating Spirits mostly came from his client Kuai Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His Records of Investigating Spirits owed much to his client Kuai Liang.

sentences.zh: 鍇所著則有文集、家傳、《方輿記》、《古今國典》、《賦苑》、《歲時廣記》云。

translations.literal: Kai's works included collected writings, family biography, Record of Regions, Ancient and Modern State Canons, Garden of Fu, and Broad Record of Seasons and Festivals.
translations.idiomatic: Kai wrote collected works, family biography, Record of Regions, state canons, Garden of Fu, and Broad Record of Seasons.

sentences.zh: 句中正，字坦然，益州華陽人。

translations.literal: Ju Zhongzheng, styled Tanran, was a native of Huayang in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Zhongzheng, courtesy name Tanran, was from Huayang in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 孟昶時，館於其相毋昭裔之第，昭裔奏授崇文館校書郎，復舉進士及第，累為昭裔從事。

translations.literal: Under Meng Chang he lodged at the mansion of Chancellor Wu Zhaoyi; Zhaoyi memorialized him as collator in the Chongwen Hall, and he again passed the jinshi and served Zhaoyi as aide.
translations.idiomatic: Under Meng Chang he lodged with Chancellor Wu Zhaoyi, became Chongwen collator and jinshi, and served Zhaoyi as aide.

sentences.zh: 歸朝，補曹州錄事參軍、汜水令，又為潞州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: On submitting to the Song court he was posted recorder in Caozhou, magistrate of Sishui, and again recorder in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Song service he was Caozhou recorder, Sishui magistrate, and Luzhou recorder.

sentences.zh: 中正精於字學，古文、篆、隸、行、草無不工。

translations.literal: Zhongzheng was expert in graphology; ancient script, seal, clerical, running, and cursive—none was not skilled.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered graphology—ancient, seal, clerical, running, and cursive alike.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，獻八體書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping xingguo (977) he presented books in eight scripts.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping xingguo 2 (977) he presented eight script styles.

sentences.zh: 太宗素聞其名，召入，授著作佐郎、直史館，被詔詳定《篇》、《韻》。

translations.literal: Taizong had long heard his name and summoned him, appointing Assistant Compiler and duty historian, and ordered him to fix the Pian and Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong summoned him as Assistant Compiler and duty historian to fix the Pian and Yun.

sentences.zh: 四年，命副張洎為高麗加恩使，還，遷左讚善大夫，改著作郎，與徐鉉重校定《說文》，模印頒行。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was ordered as deputy to Zhang Ji on the Goryeo grace mission; on return he was promoted Left Mentor, made Compiler, and with Xu Xuan again collated the Shuowen and had it carved and issued.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he deputized Zhang Ji to Goryeo, then collated the Shuowen with Xu Xuan for printing.

sentences.zh: 太宗覽之嘉賞，因問中正，凡有聲無字有幾何？

translations.literal: Taizong read it with praise and asked Zhongzheng how many sounds had no written form.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong praised it and asked how many sounds lacked graphs.

sentences.zh: 中正退，條為一卷以獻。

translations.literal: Zhongzheng withdrew and listed them in one juan for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzheng listed them in one juan.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕亦得二十一字，可並錄之也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'We also have twenty-one characters; record them together.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor added twenty-one graphs of his own for inclusion.

sentences.zh: 時又命中正與著作佐郎吳鉉、大理寺丞楊文舉同撰定《雍熙廣韻》。

translations.literal: At the time he also ordered Zhongzheng with Assistant Compiler Wu Xuan and Judicial Review Vice Director Yang Wenju jointly to compile the Yongxi Guangyun.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Zhongzheng, Wu Xuan, and Yang Wenju to compile the Yongxi Guangyun.

sentences.zh: 中正先以門類上進，麵賜緋魚，俄加太常博士。

translations.literal: Zhongzheng first presented by category and was personally given crimson fish; soon he was added Erudite of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting by category he received crimson fish and soon became Erudite of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 《廣韻》成，凡一百卷，特拜虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: When the Guangyun was finished, one hundred juan in all, he was specially made Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangyun finished at one hundred juan brought him Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 淳化元年，改直昭文館，三遷屯田郎中，杜門守道，以文翰為樂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunhua (990) he was transferred to duty in the Zhaowen Hall, thrice promoted to Director in the Court of Revenue, closed his door and kept the Way, taking literary writing as pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Chunhua 1 (990) brought Zhaowen duty and thrice promotion to Revenue Director; he kept to his study and the Way.

sentences.zh: 太宗神主及諡寶篆文，皆詔中正書之。

translations.literal: The seal script for Taizong's spirit tablet and seal of posthumous title were all ordered written by Zhongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's spirit tablet and posthumous seal script were all Zhongzheng's hand.

sentences.zh: 嘗以大小篆、八分三體書《孝經》摹石，咸平三年表上之。

translations.literal: He once copied the Classic of Filial Piety in large and small seal and eight-part scripts on stone and presented the table in the third year of Xianping (1000).
translations.idiomatic: He carved the Filial Classic in three scripts on stone and presented it in Xianping 3 (1000).

sentences.zh: 真宗召見便殿，賜坐，問所書幾許時，中正曰：「臣寫此書，十五年方成。」

translations.literal: Zhenzong summoned him to the side hall, gave him a seat, and asked how long the writing took; Zhongzheng said: 'Your servant spent fifteen years finishing this book.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong asked how long the carving took; Zhongzheng said fifteen years.

sentences.zh: 上嘉歎良久，賜金紫，命藏於秘閣。

translations.literal: The emperor praised at length and granted gold and purple, ordering it stored in the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong praised him, granted gold and purple, and stored the stones in the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 時乾州獻古銅鼎，狀方而四足，上有古文二十一字，人莫能曉，命中正與杜鎬詳驗以聞，援據甚悉。

translations.literal: At the time Qianzhou presented an ancient bronze ding, square with four legs, bearing twenty-one ancient characters no one could read; Zhongzheng and Du Gao were ordered to verify and report with full citation.
translations.idiomatic: An ancient ding from Qianzhou bore twenty-one unreadable characters; Zhongzheng and Du Gao deciphered them with full citation.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: In the fifth year (1002) he died, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year (1002) at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 中正喜藏書，家無餘財。

translations.literal: Zhongzheng loved collecting books and left no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: He collected books and died without surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 子希古、希仲並進士及第，希仲太常博士。

translations.literal: His sons Xigu and Xizhong both passed the jinshi; Xizhong was Erudite of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Xigu and Xizhong took jinshi; Xizhong became Erudite of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 蜀人又有孫逢吉、林罕。

translations.literal: Among Shu men were also Sun Fengji and Lin Han.
translations.idiomatic: Two other Shu scholars were Sun Fengji and Lin Han.

sentences.zh: 逢吉嘗為蜀國子《毛詩》博士、檢校刊刻石經。

translations.literal: Fengji had been Shu state Erudite of the Mao Odes and collator for carving the stone classics.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji was Shu Erudite of the Mao Odes and oversaw carving the stone classics.

sentences.zh: 罕亦善文字之學，嘗著《說文》二十篇，目曰《林氏小說》，刻石蜀中。

translations.literal: Han was also skilled in writing study; he once wrote twenty chapters of Shuowen titled Lin's Epitome and carved them on stone in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Han wrote twenty chapters titled Lin's Epitome from the Shuowen and carved them in Shu.

sentences.zh: 曾致堯字正臣，撫州南豐人。

translations.literal: Ceng Zhiyao, styled Zhengchen, was a native of Nanfeng in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ceng Zhiyao, courtesy name Zhengchen, was from Nanfeng in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 太平興國八年進士，解褐符離主簿、梁州錄事參軍，三遷著作佐郎、直史館，改秘書丞，出為兩浙轉運使。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the eighth year of Taiping xingguo (983), on leaving office recorder of Fuli and staff officer in Liangzhou, thrice promoted to Assistant Compiler and duty historian, made Secretariat Director, and sent out as transport commissioner of the two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping xingguo 8 (983) jinshi led to Fuli recorder, Liangzhou staff officer, Secretariat posts, and two-Zhe transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 嘗上言：「去歲所部秋租，惟湖州一郡督納及期，而蘇、常、潤三州悉有逋負，請各按賞罰。」

translations.literal: He once memorialized: 'Last year autumn rent in my circuit—only Huzhou finished on time; Suzhou, Changzhou, and Runzhou all had arrears. I ask rewards and punishments for each.'
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that only Huzhou paid autumn rent on time while Suzhou, Changzhou, and Runzhou were in arrears and asked graded rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 太宗以江、淮頻年水災，蘇、常特甚，所言刻薄不可行，詔戒致堯毋擾。

translations.literal: Taizong, because the Jiang-Huai had suffered floods year after year and Suzhou and Changzhou especially, held the words harsh and unworkable and ordered Zhiyao not to disturb.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, citing Jiang-Huai floods especially at Suzhou and Changzhou, called this harsh and told him not to disturb.

sentences.zh: 俄徙知壽州，轉太常博士。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to prefect of Shouzhou and made Erudite of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became prefect of Shouzhou and Erudite of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 致堯性剛率，好言事，前後屢上章奏，辭多激訐。

translations.literal: Zhiyao was by nature firm and forthright and liked to speak about affairs; again and again he submitted memorials, whose language was often sharp and accusatory.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyao was firm and forthright by nature and liked to discuss affairs. He repeatedly submitted memorials, often in sharp and accusatory language.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，遷主客員外郎、判鹽鐵勾院。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong ascended the throne, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of Receptions and Judge of the Salt and Iron Accounts Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong ascended the throne, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of Receptions and Judge of the Salt and Iron Accounts Office.

sentences.zh: 張齊賢薦其材，任詞職，命翰林試制誥，既而以輿議未允而罷。

translations.literal: Zhang Qixian recommended his talent for a drafting post and ordered that he be tested in drafting edicts in the Hanlin Academy, but before long, because public opinion did not approve, it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qixian recommended his talent for a drafting post and had him tested in the Hanlin Academy on drafting edicts, but the appointment was soon abandoned because public opinion did not approve.

sentences.zh: 李繼遷擾西鄙，靈武危急，命張齊賢為涇、原、邠、寧、環、慶等州經略使，選致堯為判官，仍遷戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: Li Jiqian harassed the western border and Lingwu was critical; Zhang Qixian was made commissioner for Jing, Yuan, Bin, Ning, Huan, and Qing circuits and Zhiyao was chosen as aide, still promoted Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: With Li Jiqian threatening the west, Zhang Qixian became frontier commissioner and chose Zhiyao as aide with promotion to Revenue Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 既受命，因抗疏自陳，願不受章紱之賜，詞旨狂躁。

translations.literal: Having received the order, he submitted a bold memorial on his own behalf wishing not to receive seal and ribbon rewards; the wording was wild and rash.
translations.idiomatic: He boldly refused seal and ribbon rewards in wild, rash wording.

sentences.zh: 詔御史府鞫其罪，黜為黃州副使，奪金紫。

translations.literal: The court ordered the censorate to try his crime; he was demoted to vice commissioner of Huangzhou and stripped of gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate demoted him to Huangzhou vice commissioner and stripped gold and purple.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復舊官，改吏部員外郎，曆知泰、泉、蘇、揚、鄂五州。

translations.literal: Before long his former rank was restored; he was made Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel and in succession was prefect of Tai, Quan, Su, Yang, and Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon restored, he became Personnel Vice Director and prefect of Tai, Quan, Su, Yang, and E.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，遷禮部郎中，坐知揚州日冒請一月奉，降掌升州榷酤，轉戶部郎中。

translations.literal: In early Dazhong xiangfu he was promoted Director in the Ministry of Rites; for falsely claiming one month's salary as Yangzhou prefect he was demoted to manage Shengzhou liquor monopoly and became Revenue Director.
translations.idiomatic: Early Dazhong xiangfu brought Rites Director; a false salary claim as Yangzhou prefect demoted him to Shengzhou liquor monopoly then Revenue Director.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: In the fifth year (1012) he died, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year (1012) at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 致堯頗好纂錄，所著有《仙鳧習翼》三十卷、《廣中台志》八十卷、《清邊前要》三十卷、《西陲要紀》十卷、《為臣要紀》一十五篇。

translations.literal: Zhiyao greatly loved compilation; his works include Immortal Cranes Practicing Wings in thirty juan, Record of the Broad Central Terrace in eighty juan, Essentials of Clearing the Frontier in thirty juan, Record of the Western Border in ten juan, and Essentials for Ministers in fifteen pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Immortal Cranes Practicing Wings (30 juan), Record of the Broad Central Terrace (80 juan), and other frontier and ministerial works.

sentences.zh: 子易從、易占皆登進士第。

translations.literal: His sons Yicong and Yizhan both passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Yicong and Yizhan both took jinshi.

sentences.zh: 刁衎，字元賓，昇州人。

translations.literal: Diao Kan, styled Yuanbin, was a native of Shengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Kan, courtesy name Yuanbin, was from Shengzhou.

sentences.zh: 父彥能，仕南唐為昭武軍節度。

translations.literal: His father Yanneng served Southern Tang as military commissioner of Zhaowu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanneng was Southern Tang military commissioner of Zhaowu.

sentences.zh: 衎用蔭為秘書郎、集賢校理，衣五品服，以文翰入侍，甚被親昵。

translations.literal: By yin privilege Kan was Secretariat secretary and Hongwen collator, wearing fifth-rank dress, entering attendance for literary writing and greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: By yin privilege he was Secretariat secretary and Hongwen collator in fifth-rank dress, favored for literary attendance.

sentences.zh: 李煜嘗令直清輝殿，閱中外章奏。

translations.literal: Li Yu once ordered him on duty in the Qinghui Hall to review internal and external memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu had him review memorials in the Qinghui Hall.

sentences.zh: 金陵平，從煜歸宋，太祖賜緋魚，授太常寺太祝。

translations.literal: When Jinling fell he followed Yu to Song; Taizu granted crimson fish and appointed him Grand Sacrificer in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinling's fall he followed Yu to Song; Taizu made him Grand Sacrificer.

sentences.zh: 稱疾，假滿，屏居輦下者數歲。

translations.literal: Pleading illness, when leave expired he lived in seclusion below the capital for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Pleading illness he lived in seclusion near the capital for years.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，李昉、扈蒙在翰林，勉其出仕，因撰《聖德頌》獻之。

translations.literal: In early Taiping xingguo Li Fang and Hu Meng were in the Hanlin and urged him to take office; he composed and presented 'Ode to Sagely Virtue.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Fang and Hu Meng urged him out; he presented an Ode to Sagely Virtue.

sentences.zh: 詔復本官，出知睦州桐廬縣。

translations.literal: An edict restored his former post and he went out as magistrate of Tonglu in Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored and sent as Tonglu magistrate in Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 會詔群臣言事，衎上《諫刑書》，謂：

translations.literal: When the court ordered all officials to speak on affairs, Kan submitted 'Memorial on Punishment' saying:
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to speak on policy he submitted a Memorial on Punishment:

sentences.zh: 淫刑酷法非律文所載者，望詔天下悉禁止之。

translations.literal: Lewd punishments and harsh laws not recorded in the statutes—I hope Your Majesty will order the empire to forbid them all.
translations.idiomatic: Lewd punishments not in the statutes should be forbidden empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 巡檢使臣捕得盜賊、亡卒，並送本部法官訊鞫，無得擅加酷虐。

translations.literal: Patrol commissioners who capture bandits and deserters must send them to headquarters judges for examination and must not on their own add cruel torture.
translations.idiomatic: Patrols must send captives to headquarters judges without adding torture.

sentences.zh: 古者投奸凶於四裔，今遠方囚人盡歸京闕，以配務役，最非其宜。

translations.literal: Antiquity cast the wicked to the four borders; today distant prisoners all come to the capital for corvée—this is most unsuitable.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity banished the wicked to the borders; today distant prisoners labor at the capital—most unsuitable.

sentences.zh: 且神皋勝地，天子所居，豈使流囚於此聚役。

translations.literal: The divine region is where the Son of Heaven dwells—how can flowing prisoners be gathered here for labor?
translations.idiomatic: The imperial capital is no place to gather exiled laborers.

sentences.zh: 自今外處罪人，望勿許解送上京，亦不留於諸務充役。

translations.literal: From today criminals from outer regions should not be sent up to the capital nor kept in various offices for corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth outer criminals should not be sent to the capital or kept for corvée.

sentences.zh: 又《禮》曰：「刑人於市，與眾棄之。」

translations.literal: The Rites also says: 'Punish men in the market and abandon them with the multitude.'
translations.idiomatic: The Rites say: punish men in the market and abandon them with the multitude.'

sentences.zh: 則知黃屋紫宸之中，非用刑行法之處。

translations.literal: Then one knows the yellow canopy and purple hall are not places for applying punishment and law.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial hall is no place for punishment.

sentences.zh: 望自今御前不行決罰之刑，殿前引見司鉗黥法具，並赴御史臺、廷尉之獄；

translations.literal: I hope from today capital punishment is not carried out before the throne; the instruments of the Palace Reception Office for branding and shackling should all go to the censorate and court prison;
translations.idiomatic: Capital punishment should not occur before the throne; branding tools should go to the censorate and court prison;

sentences.zh: 敕杖不以大小，皆引赴御史、廷尉。

translations.literal: imperial caning, large or small, should all be conducted at the censorate and court prison.
translations.idiomatic: imperial beatings should be conducted at the censorate and court prison.

sentences.zh: 京府或出中使，或命法官，具禮監科，以重聖皇明刑慎法之意。
