translations.literal: The capital prefecture may send inner envoys or appoint judges with full ritual oversight to weight the sage's intent of bright punishment and cautious law.
translations.idiomatic: The capital should use envoys or judges with ritual oversight to show cautious punishment.

sentences.zh: 或有犯劫盜亡命，罪重者刖足釘身，國門布令。

translations.literal: Some who commit robbery or desertion with heavy guilt have feet cut and bodies nailed, with proclamation at the national gate.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy robbers and deserters suffer foot-cutting and nailing with proclamation at the gate.

sentences.zh: 此乃小民昧於刑憲，逼於衣食，偶然為惡，義不及他，被其慘毒，實傷風化，亦望減除其法。

translations.literal: These are common men ignorant of penal statutes, pressed by food and clothing, who occasionally do evil without reaching further; such cruelty truly harms transformation—I also hope to reduce this law.
translations.idiomatic: Petty offenders driven by hunger suffer cruel display that harms mores—I ask this law be reduced.

sentences.zh: 如此則人情不駭，各固其生；

translations.literal: Thus men's hearts would not be terrified and each would secure his life;
translations.idiomatic: Then hearts would not be terrified and each would secure life;

sentences.zh: 和氣無傷，必臻上瑞。

translations.literal: harmony would not be injured and supreme auspices would surely arrive.
translations.idiomatic: harmony uninjured, supreme auspices would arrive.

sentences.zh: 再遷大理寺丞，獻文四十篇。

translations.literal: Twice promoted to Vice Director in the Court of Judicial Review, he presented forty pieces of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Twice promoted in Judicial Review he presented forty writings.

sentences.zh: 召試，授殿中丞、通判湖州，上疏請定天下酒稅額、修郡縣城隍、條約牧宰、除兩浙丁身錢、禁汴水流屍，凡五事。

translations.literal: Summoned for examination, he was appointed Palace Attendant and military commissioner of Huzhou, and memorialized to fix empire-wide liquor tax quotas, repair prefectural walls, set rules for magistrates, abolish two-Zhe head tax, and forbid corpses in the Bian River—five items in all.
translations.idiomatic: Examined as Palace Attendant and Huzhou commissioner, he asked to fix liquor taxes, repair walls, regulate magistrates, abolish two-Zhe head tax, and forbid Bian corpses.

sentences.zh: 俄知婺州，遷國子博士。

translations.literal: Soon he was made prefect of Wuzhou and promoted Erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He became Wuzhou prefect and Directorate Erudite.

sentences.zh: 會考校百官殿最，衎被召，以無過，得知光州，就改虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: When officials' merits were examined Kan was summoned; as he had no fault he was made prefect of Guangzhou and at once changed to Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Merit review found no fault; he became Guangzhou prefect then Rites Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 轉運使狀其政績，優詔嘉獎，徙知廬州。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner reported his achievements; an excellent edict praised him and he was moved to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His transport commissioner praised him; an edict commended him and he moved to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，遷比部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong succeeded he was promoted Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong's accession brought Revenue Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 嘗上疏曰：

translations.literal: He once memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized:

sentences.zh: 臣聞天下，大器也；

translations.literal: Your servant hears that the empire is a great vessel;
translations.idiomatic: The empire is a great vessel;

sentences.zh: 群生，眾畜也。

translations.literal: the multitude are many beasts.
translations.idiomatic: the people are many beasts.

sentences.zh: 治大器者執一以正其度，保眾畜者齊化以臻其原。

translations.literal: To govern a great vessel one holds to one standard to set its measure; to preserve many beasts one harmonizes transformation to reach their source.
translations.idiomatic: Governing the vessel requires one standard; preserving the herd requires harmonizing transformation.

sentences.zh: 故至人謂莫神於天，莫富於地，莫大於帝王。

translations.literal: Hence the perfected say nothing is more spiritlike than Heaven, nothing richer than Earth, nothing greater than emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: The perfected say nothing surpasses Heaven, Earth, or the emperor.

sentences.zh: 又曰：帝王乘地而總萬物，以用人也。

translations.literal: They also say emperors and kings ride Earth and marshal the myriad things through employing men.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors ride Earth and marshal all things by employing men.

sentences.zh: 則知萬乘之尊，一人之位，等天地之覆燾，若日月之照臨，可不慎思慮以安民，係慘舒而被物！

translations.literal: Then one knows the honor of ten thousand chariots and the position of one man equal Heaven and Earth's covering nurture, like sun and moon shining—how can one not carefully think to settle the people and bind joy and sorrow to cover things!
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven equals Heaven and Earth's nurture; he must think carefully to settle the people.

sentences.zh: 所以堯、舜篤善道以垂化，而民謂之所天；

translations.literal: Therefore Yao and Shun pursued the good Way to hand down transformation, and the people called them what-is-Heaven;
translations.idiomatic: Yao and Shun pursued the good Way and the people called them Heaven;

sentences.zh: 桀、紂懷凶德以害世，而民謂之獨夫。

translations.literal: Jie and Zhou harbored vicious virtue to harm the age, and the people called them lone men.
translations.idiomatic: Jie and Zhou harmed the age and the people called them lone men.

sentences.zh: 則君之於民，善惡有如是之驗；

translations.literal: Thus the ruler's relation to the people has such proof in good and evil;
translations.idiomatic: Rulers' good and evil prove themselves thus in the people;

sentences.zh: 民之於君，毀譽有如是之異。

translations.literal: the people's praise and blame toward the ruler have such difference.
translations.idiomatic: the people's praise and blame differ thus toward rulers.

sentences.zh: 陛下纂圖茲始，布政惟新，所宜上順天心，下從人欲，進善以去惡，避毀而求譽。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has begun to inherit the chart and spread new government; you should above follow Heaven's heart and below follow men's desires, advance good and remove evil, avoid blame and seek praise.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty inherits the chart anew; follow Heaven's heart and men's desires, advance good, remove evil.

sentences.zh: 遵唐、虞之治，斥辛、癸之亂，私賞無及於小人，私罰無施於君子，任賢勿貳，去邪勿疑。

translations.literal: Follow the rule of Tang and Yu, reject the disorder of Xin and Gui; private rewards should not reach petty men, private punishments should not touch gentlemen; employ the worthy without doubt, remove the wicked without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Follow Tang and Yu, reject Xin and Gui; reward not petty men, punish not gentlemen; employ worthies, remove the wicked.

sentences.zh: 開諫諍之門，塞讒佞之口，愛而知其惡，憎而知其善，無以春秋鼎盛而耽於逸遊，無以血氣方剛而惑於聲色。

translations.literal: Open the gate of remonstrance, stop the mouth of slanderers; love yet know their evil, hate yet know their good; do not because spring and autumn are at their height indulge in roaming; do not because blood and qi are strong be deluded by sound and color.
translations.idiomatic: Open remonstrance, stop slander; love yet know evil, hate yet know good; do not roam in prime years nor be deluded by pleasure.

sentences.zh: 若太祖之勤儉，若太宗之惠慈，答天地敷錫之意，保祖宗艱難之業，則周成、漢文二宗之美，不可同年而議擬也。

translations.literal: If like Taizu in frugality, like Taizong in kindness, answering Heaven and Earth's abundant gift and preserving the ancestors' hard-won enterprise, then the beauties of Zhou Cheng and Han Wen cannot be matched in the same year.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu's frugality and Taizong's kindness answering Heaven would rival Zhou Cheng and Han Wen.

sentences.zh: 代還，獻所著《本說》十卷，得以本官充秘閣校理，出知潁州。

translations.literal: On returning from term he presented his Basic Discourse in ten juan and was allowed to fill his post as Secret Archive collator, going out as prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Returning he presented Basic Discourse in ten juan, became Secret Archive collator, and went to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為比部員外郎，改直秘閣，充崇文院檢討。

translations.literal: He entered as Revenue Vice Director, changed to duty in the Secret Archive, and filled Chongwen collation.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as Revenue Vice Director, took Secret Archive duty, and collated at Chongwen.

sentences.zh: 時杜鎬、陳彭年並預檢討、衎言此二人可專其任，詔許解職，判三司開拆司，預修《冊府元龜》，加主客郎中。

translations.literal: At the time Du Gao and Chen Pengnian were also collating; Kan said these two could specialize in the task; an edict allowed him to leave the post, judge the Three Offices Opening and Inspection Office, take part in compiling the Prime Archive of the Imperial Library, and was added Director in the Court of Imperial Guests.
translations.idiomatic: He yielded collation to Du Gao and Chen Pengnian, judged the Three Offices, helped compile the Prime Archive, and became Guests Director.

sentences.zh: 求領外任，得知湖州，轉刑部郎中。

translations.literal: Seeking outer appointment he was made prefect of Huzhou and became Punishments Director.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking the provinces he became Huzhou prefect and Punishments Director.

sentences.zh: 歲滿，復預編修。

translations.literal: When his term expired he again took part in compilation.
translations.idiomatic: At term's end he returned to compilation.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符六年，書成，授兵部郎中。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dazhong xiangfu (1013) when the book was finished he was appointed Punishments Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong xiangfu 6 (1013) the book finished and he became War Punishments Director.

sentences.zh: 入朝，暴中風眩，真宗遣使馳賜金丹，已不救，年六十九。

translations.literal: On entering court he suddenly suffered a stroke with vertigo; Emperor Zhenzong sent an envoy posthaste to bestow golden pills, but they could not save him. He was sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court he was stricken with sudden vertigo from a stroke. Emperor Zhenzong dispatched a courier with golden elixirs, yet nothing could save him. He died at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 衎始仕李氏，權勢甚盛。

translations.literal: At first Kang served the Li regime, whose power was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Kang had begun his career under the Li dynasty, when that house still held enormous power.

sentences.zh: 父為藩帥，家富於財，被服飲膳，極於侈靡。

translations.literal: His father was a military governor; the family was rich in wealth, and their dress, food, and drink were carried to the utmost extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: His father had been a frontier commander, and the household was immensely wealthy—its clothing, fare, and table were carried to the height of luxury.

sentences.zh: 歸宋，以純澹夷雅知名於時，恬於祿位，善談笑，喜棋弈，交道敦篤，士大夫多推重之。

translations.literal: After returning to Song, he became known in his time for pure simplicity and refined ease; he was indifferent to salary and rank, skilled in banter, fond of chess, sincere in friendship, and many scholar-officials held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Once he entered Song service, he won renown for plain dignity and quiet grace. Indifferent to office and emolument, easy in conversation, devoted to chess, and steadfast in his friendships, he was widely respected among the literati.

sentences.zh: 子湛、湜、渭，皆登進士第。

translations.literal: His sons Zhan, Shi, and Wei all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zhan, Shi, and Wei all earned jinshi degrees.

sentences.zh: 湛，刑部郎中；

translations.literal: Zhan was Director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan rose to Director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 湜，屯田員外；

translations.literal: Shi was an Outer-Director in the Directorate of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: Shi served as Outer-Director in the Directorate of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 渭，太常博士。

translations.literal: Wei was an Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Wei held the post of Erudite in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 湛子繹、約，天聖中並進士及第。

translations.literal: Zhan's sons Yi and Yue both passed the jinshi examination in the Tiansheng era.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's sons Yi and Yue both took jinshi degrees during the Tiansheng reign.

sentences.zh: 姚鉉，字寶之，廬州合肥人。

translations.literal: Yao Xuan, styled Baozhi, was a native of Hefei in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xuan, courtesy name Baozhi, came from Hefei in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 太平興國八年進士甲科，解褐大理評事，知潭州湘鄉縣，三遷殿中丞，通判簡、宣、升三州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taiping xingguo he passed the jinshi examination in the top class; on leaving office he was made investigating clerk in the Court of Judicial Review and prefect of Xiangxiang County in Tanzhou; after three promotions he became Palace Director and served as military prefect of Jian, Xuan, and Sheng prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping xingguo 8 he graduated jinshi in the highest tier, entered service as a judicial reviewer, and governed Xiangxiang in Tanzhou. Three promotions later he was Palace Director and military prefect in turn of Jian, Xuan, and Sheng.

sentences.zh: 淳化五年，直史館，侍宴內苑，應製賦《賞花釣魚詩》，特被嘉賞，翌日，命中使就第賜白金以獎之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunhua he was appointed duty scholar in the Historiography Institute; attending a banquet in the inner park, he composed on command the poem "On Enjoying Flowers and Angling for Fish" and received special commendation. The next day the emperor ordered a palace envoy to visit his residence and bestow white gold as a reward.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 5 he became a duty scholar in the Historiography Institute. At an inner-garden banquet he wrote on command the poem "On Enjoying Flowers and Angling for Fish," won exceptional praise, and on the following day received a palace envoy at his home bearing a reward of white gold.

sentences.zh: 至道初，遷太常丞，充京西轉運使，曆右正言、右司諫、河東轉運使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhidao era he was promoted to Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and appointed transport commissioner for the Jingxi circuit; he then served as Right Remonstrator, Right Remonstrator of the Department of State Affairs, and transport commissioner for the Hedong circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhidao he rose to Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and transport commissioner for Jingxi, then served as Right Remonstrator, Right Remonstrator in the Department of State Affairs, and Hedong transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 俄上言曰：「伏見諸路官吏，或強明蒞事、惠愛及民者，則必立教條，除其煩擾。

translations.literal: Before long he submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject observes that among officials on the various circuits, when any are forceful and clear in handling affairs and extend kindness to the people, they invariably establish regulations and remove vexatious burdens.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he memorialized: "I observe that whenever a circuit official governs with forceful clarity and genuine care for the people, he sets down regulations and clears away petty harassment.

sentences.zh: 然狡胥之輩，非其所便，俟其罷官，悉藏記籍，害公蠹政，莫甚於此。

translations.literal: Yet the crafty clerks, finding these inconvenient, wait until he leaves office and then hide all the record books—harm to the public and rot in government, nothing is worse than this.
translations.idiomatic: But the shrewd clerks, disliking the change, wait until he departs and then conceal the registers—no plague on public business runs deeper.

sentences.zh: 《禮》云：『其人存則其政舉，其人亡則其政息。』

translations.literal: The Rites says: 'When the man remains, his policies stand; when the man is gone, his policies cease.'
translations.idiomatic: The Rites states: 'While the man remains, his policies endure; when he is gone, they vanish.'

sentences.zh: 又《語》曰：『舊令尹之政必告新令尹。』

translations.literal: The Analects also says: 'The policies of the old magistrate must be reported to the new magistrate.'
translations.idiomatic: And the Analects adds: 'The outgoing magistrate's policies must be handed on to his successor.'

sentences.zh: 斯實聖人之格言，國家之急務也。

translations.literal: These are truly maxims of the sages and urgent affairs of the state.
translations.idiomatic: These are sage precepts and matters the state cannot neglect.

sentences.zh: 欲望所在官吏，有經畫利濟事可長久者，歲終書曆，受代日錄付新官，俾之遵守。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes that wherever officials have planned measures of lasting benefit, they write them in a yearly record and, on the day they hand over office, deliver the record to the incoming official so that he may observe and keep them.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that whenever an official devises a measure of lasting public benefit, he enter it in an annual record and, on relinquishing his post, deliver that record to his successor for faithful observance.

sentences.zh: 若事有灼然匪便，聽上聞，俟報改正。」

translations.literal: If any matter is plainly unsuitable, he may be permitted to report upward and await orders before correcting it."
translations.idiomatic: If a measure is clearly unworkable, the successor may report upward and amend it only after receiving approval.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，河決鄆州王陵埽，東南注钜野，入淮、泗，城中積水壞廬舍，以鉉知州事，徙州於汶陽鄉之高原，委以營度，許便宜從事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping the Yellow River broke through the Wangling embankment in Yanzhou and poured southeast into Juye, entering the Huai and Si; water accumulated in the city and ruined houses. Xuan was put in charge of the prefecture, the seat was moved to the high ground at Wenyang township, and he was entrusted with planning and construction, with authority to act as expedient required.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 3 the Yellow River burst the Wangling levee in Yanzhou and flooded southeast into Juye and on toward the Huai and Si. Water stood in the city and wrecked dwellings. Xuan was assigned to govern the prefecture, relocate the seat to the heights at Wenyang township, and oversee the works with full discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 工畢，加起居舍人、京東轉運使，徙兩浙路。

translations.literal: When the work was finished he was made Drafting Attendant and transport commissioner for the Jingdong circuit, then transferred to the Liang-Zhe circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After the project was complete he became Drafting Attendant and Jingdong transport commissioner, then moved to the Liang-Zhe circuit.

sentences.zh: 鉉雋爽，頗尚氣。

translations.literal: Xuan was sharp and forthright and rather given to spirited pride.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was quick-witted and outspoken, with a touch of proud temper.

sentences.zh: 薛映知杭州，與之不協，事多矛盾。

translations.literal: When Xue Ying governed Hangzhou, the two were not in accord and their affairs often clashed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xue Ying's prefecture at Hangzhou they fell out, and their business repeatedly collided.

sentences.zh: 映摭鉉罪狀數條，密以聞，詔使劾之，當奪一官，特除名，貶連州文學。

translations.literal: Ying collected several counts of Xuan's offenses and reported them secretly; the court ordered an investigation. The penalty should have been reduction by one rank, but he was specially stripped of office and demoted to literary instructor in Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ying gathered several charges against Xuan and sent them in secret. An imperial inquiry followed; though the statutory penalty was demotion by one rank, he was specially removed from the rolls and exiled as literary instructor in Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 吉州之萬安抵虔，江有贛石，舟行其中，湍險萬狀，鉉過，感而賦之以自況。

translations.literal: From Wan'an in Jizhou to Qian the river held the Gan rocks; boats passing among them faced a myriad dangers. When Xuan crossed, moved by the scene he composed a poem to reflect his own plight.
translations.idiomatic: Between Wan'an in Jizhou and Qian lay the Gan rocks, where river traffic met a thousand perils. Crossing them, Xuan was stirred to verse that mirrored his own fall from favor.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符五年，會赦，移岳州，又移舒州，俄授本州團練副使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dazhong xiangfu, when an amnesty was proclaimed, he was moved to Yuezhou, then to Shuzhou, and soon afterward appointed deputy militia commissioner of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong xiangfu 5, upon a general amnesty, he was transferred to Yuezhou and then Shuzhou, and shortly thereafter named deputy militia commissioner there.

sentences.zh: 天禧四年卒，年五十三。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianxi he died, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Tianxi 4 at fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 鉉文辭敏麗，善筆劄，藏書至多，頗有異本，兩浙課吏寫書，亦薛映所掎之一事。

translations.literal: Xuan's literary style was quick and elegant; he was skilled in letters and possessed an enormous library with many rare editions. The Liang-Zhe clerks' duty of copying books was also one of the points on which Xue Ying had picked at him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan wrote with swift grace and handled correspondence with ease. His library was vast and held many unusual texts; the Liang-Zhe clerks' book-copying duty was itself one of the grievances Xue Ying had raised against him.

sentences.zh: 雖被竄斥，猶傭夫荷擔以自隨。

translations.literal: Even after his banishment he still kept hired porters to carry his books wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: Even in exile he traveled with hired bearers hauling his books.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collection in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 又采唐人文章纂為百卷，目曰《文粹》。

translations.literal: He also compiled Tang prose into one hundred juan, entitled Literary Essence.
translations.idiomatic: He also anthologized Tang prose in one hundred juan under the title Literary Essence.

sentences.zh: 卒後，子嗣復以其書上獻，詔藏內府，授嗣復永城主簿。

translations.literal: After his death his son Sifu presented the book to the throne; an edict ordered it stored in the inner treasury, and Sifu was appointed registrar of Yongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his son Sifu offered the anthology to the court. It was ordered into the inner library, and Sifu was made registrar of Yongcheng.

sentences.zh: 幼子稱，俊穎美秀，頗善屬辭，裁十歲卒。

translations.literal: His youngest son Cheng was handsome and bright and quite able at composition, but died at only ten.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Cheng was handsome, clever, and already skilled in writing, yet died at ten.

sentences.zh: 鉉紀其事為《聰悟錄》，人多傳之。

translations.literal: Xuan recorded the affair in Record of Precocious Understanding, which many people circulated.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan set the story down in Record of Precocious Understanding, and it was widely copied.

sentences.zh: 李建中，字得中，其先京兆人。

translations.literal: Li Jianzhong, styled Dezong, was originally a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jianzhong, courtesy name Dezong, traced his origins to Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖逢，唐左衛兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Feng was Army Adjutant of the Left Guard in Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Feng had been Army Adjutant of the Left Guard under Tang.

sentences.zh: 祖稠，梁商州刺史，避地入蜀。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chou was prefect of Shangzhou under Liang and fled into Shu to escape turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chou, Shangzhou prefect under Later Liang, took refuge in Shu amid the upheavals.

sentences.zh: 會王建僭據，稠預佐命功臣，左衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Wang Jian seized power, Chou was counted among the founding ministers and made General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jian established his rule, Chou was honored as a founding supporter and appointed General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 建中幼好學，十四丁外艱。

translations.literal: Jianzhong loved learning from childhood and at fourteen completed mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhong had loved study since boyhood and at fourteen finished mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 會蜀平，侍母居洛陽，聚學以自給。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified he attended his mother in Luoyang and gathered pupils to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Shu he kept his mother company in Luoyang and earned a living by gathering students.

sentences.zh: 攜文遊京師，為王佑所延譽，館於石熙載之第，熙載厚待之。

translations.literal: Carrying his writings he traveled to the capital, was praised by Wang You, lodged at the residence of Shi Xizai, and was treated generously by Xizai.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the capital with his writings in hand, won recommendation from Wang You, and was housed at Shi Xizai's residence, where Xizai treated him with great kindness.

sentences.zh: 太平興國八年進士甲科，解褐大理評事，知岳州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taiping xingguo he passed the jinshi examination in the top class; on leaving office he was made investigating clerk in the Court of Judicial Review and recorder in Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping xingguo 8 he graduated jinshi in the highest tier, entered service as a judicial reviewer, and became recorder in Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 轉運使李惟清薦其能，再遷著作佐郎、監潭州茶場，改殿中丞，曆通判道、郢二州。

translations.literal: Transport commissioner Li Weiqing recommended his ability; after two promotions he was made Assistant Archivist and supervisor of the Tanzhou tea depot, then promoted to Palace Director and served in turn as military prefect of Dao and Ying prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Li Weiqing commended his talent. Two promotions later he was Assistant Archivist and overseer of the Tanzhou tea depot, then Palace Director and military prefect in turn of Dao and Ying.

sentences.zh: 柴成務領漕運，再表稱薦，轉太常博士。

translations.literal: Chai Chengwu, heading grain transport, twice submitted memorials commending him, and he was transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Chengwu, in charge of grain transport, twice memorialized in his favor, and he was made Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 時言事者多以權利進，建中表陳時政利害，序王霸之略，太宗嘉賞，因引對便殿，賜以緋魚。

translations.literal: At the time many who spoke on affairs advanced through factional interest; Jianzhong submitted a memorial setting forth the harms and benefits of current policy and outlining the strategy of true kingship and hegemony. The Taizong emperor commended this and summoned him for audience in the side hall, bestowing the scarlet robe and fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: Many who petitioned on state affairs then rose by trading on power and profit. Jianzhong memorialized on the costs and gains of current policy and laid out the principles of kingship and hegemony. Taizong praised him, received him in the side hall, and granted the scarlet robe and fish tally.

sentences.zh: 會考課京朝官，建中舊坐公累罰金，漏其事，坐降授殿中丞，監在京榷易院。

translations.literal: When the capital officials were evaluated, Jianzhong had formerly been fined for a public offense but omitted the matter; for this he was demoted to Palace Director and made supervisor of the capital monopoly exchange office.
translations.idiomatic: During the capital-official review, Jianzhong had once been fined for a public offense but failed to report it. He was therefore reduced to Palace Director and assigned to supervise the capital monopoly exchange office.

sentences.zh: 蘇易簡方被恩顧，多得對，嘗言蜀中文士，因及建中，太宗亦素知之，命直昭文館。

translations.literal: Su Yijian was then in imperial favor and often gained audiences; once, speaking of literary men from Shu, he mentioned Jianzhong, whom the Taizong emperor had long known. An order appointed him duty scholar in the Zhaowen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yijian then enjoyed the emperor's favor and often spoke at court. On one occasion, discussing Shu literati, he named Jianzhong, whom Taizong already knew well. Jianzhong was ordered to serve as duty scholar in the Zhaowen Hall.

sentences.zh: 建中父名昭文，懇辭，改集賢院。

translations.literal: Jianzhong's father was named Zhaowen; he earnestly declined and was reassigned to the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father's name was Zhaowen, Jianzhong begged off the post and was transferred to the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 數月，出為兩浙轉運副使，再遷主客員外郎，曆通判河南府，知曹、解、潁、蔡四州。

translations.literal: Several months later he went out as deputy transport commissioner for the Liang-Zhe circuit, was promoted again to Outer-Director in the Ministry of Rites, and served in turn as military prefect of Henan prefecture and as prefect of Cao, Xie, Ying, and Cai.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later he became deputy transport commissioner for Liang-Zhe, then Outer-Director in the Ministry of Rites, military prefect of Henan, and in turn prefect of Cao, Xie, Ying, and Cai.

sentences.zh: 景德中，以久次，進金部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the Jingde era, by length of service, he was promoted to Outer-Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingde, by seniority, he rose to Outer-Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 建中性簡靜，風神雅秀，恬於榮利，前後三求掌西京留司御史臺，尤愛洛中風土，就構園池，號曰「靜居」。

translations.literal: Jianzhong was by nature simple and quiet, with an elegant bearing; he was indifferent to glory and gain. Three times he sought charge of the Western Capital censorate; he especially loved the customs and landscape of Luoyang, built a garden and pond there, and called it "Quiet Dwelling."
translations.idiomatic: Simple and serene by nature, Jianzhong carried himself with refined grace and cared little for rank or profit. Thrice he asked to head the Western Capital censorate. He loved Luoyang's air and scenery above all, laid out a garden there, and named it Quiet Dwelling.

sentences.zh: 好吟詠，每遊山水，多留題，自稱岩夫民伯。

translations.literal: He loved composing and reciting poetry; whenever he toured mountains and rivers he left many inscribed poems, styling himself Yanfu Minbo.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to compose and chant verse; on every excursion among hills and streams he left poems inscribed on the scenery, and styled himself Yanfu Minbo—the Rock Hermit and Common Elder.

sentences.zh: 加司封員外郎、工部郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Outer-Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Outer-Director in the Ministry of Personnel and Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 建中善修養之術，會命官校定《道藏》，建中預焉。

translations.literal: Jianzhong was skilled in the arts of self-cultivation; when the court ordered officials to collate the Daoist Canon, Jianzhong took part.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhong practiced the arts of nourishing life. When the throne ordered a revision of the Daoist Canon, he joined the commission.

sentences.zh: 又判太府寺。

translations.literal: He also served concurrently as director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He also held concurrent appointment as director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符五年冬，命使泗州，奉御製《汴水發願文》，就致設醮。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year of Dazhong xiangfu he was ordered as envoy to Sizhou to deliver the imperially composed Vow Text on the Bian River and there conduct a ritual offering.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Dazhong xiangfu 5 he was sent to Sizhou to present the emperor's Vow Text on the Bian River and perform a ritual offering on the spot.

sentences.zh: 使還得疾，明年卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: On returning from the mission he fell ill and died the following year, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He took ill on his return from the mission and died the next year at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 建中善書劄，行筆尤工，多構新體，草、隸、篆、籀、八分亦妙，人多摹習，爭取以為楷法。

translations.literal: Jianzhong was skilled in letters; his running script was especially fine. He devised many new forms, and his draft, clerical, seal, large-seal, and eight-part scripts were all excellent. Many people copied him and competed to take his hand as their model.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhong excelled at correspondence, above all in running script. He invented many new styles, and his draft, clerical, seal, large-seal, and eight-part scripts were all masterly. Scribes copied him in crowds and took his hand as the standard.

sentences.zh: 嘗手寫郭忠恕《汗簡集》以獻，皆科斗文字，有詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: He once copied by hand Guo Zhongshu's Sweat-Bamboo Collection and presented it; all were tadpole script, and an edict commended the gift.
translations.idiomatic: He once copied out Guo Zhongshu's Sweat-Bamboo Collection and offered it to the throne—all in tadpole script—and received an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 好古勤學，多藏古器名畫。

translations.literal: He loved antiquity, studied diligently, and collected many ancient vessels and famous paintings.
translations.idiomatic: He cherished the past, studied hard, and amassed a great store of antique bronzes and celebrated paintings.

sentences.zh: 有集三十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collection in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings filled thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 子周道、周士並進士及第。

translations.literal: His sons Zhoudao and Zhoushi both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zhoudao and Zhoushi both earned jinshi degrees.

sentences.zh: 周士曆侍御史、江東、陝西轉運、三司鹽鐵判官，賜金紫，終工部郎中。

translations.literal: Zhoushi served in turn as censor, transport commissioner for Jiangdong and Shaanxi, and salt-and-iron commissioner in the Three Departments; he was granted the gold-and-purple insignia and ended as Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Zhoushi rose through service as censor, Jiangdong and Shaanxi transport commissioner, and salt-and-iron commissioner in the Three Departments. He received the gold-and-purple insignia and ended his career as Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 周民，太子中舍。

translations.literal: Zhoumin was a Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhoumin served as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 洪湛，字惟清，升州上元人。

translations.literal: Hong Zhan, styled Weiqing, was a native of Shangyuan in Shengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Zhan, courtesy name Weiqing, came from Shangyuan in Shengzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖勳，南唐崇文館直學士。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xun was a direct scholar of the Chongwen Hall under Southern Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xun had been a direct scholar in the Chongwen Hall under Southern Tang.

sentences.zh: 祖壽，桐城令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shou was magistrate of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shou served as magistrate of Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 父慶元，獻書李煜，授奉禮郎，補新喻令。

translations.literal: His father Qingyuan submitted writings to Li Yu, was appointed Master of Ceremonies, and was made magistrate of Xinyu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qingyuan presented writings to Li Yu, received appointment as Master of Ceremonies, and became magistrate of Xinyu.

sentences.zh: 歸宋，至冤句令。

translations.literal: After returning to Song he rose to magistrate of Yuanqu.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Song service he advanced to magistrate of Yuanqu.

sentences.zh: 湛幼好學，五歲能為詩，未冠，錄所著十卷為《齠年集》。

translations.literal: Zhan loved learning from childhood; at five he could compose poetry, and before reaching adulthood he compiled ten juan of his writings under the title Collection of Early Youth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan loved study from childhood. At five he could write poems, and before coming of age he gathered ten juan of his work as Collection of Early Youth.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，有聲。

translations.literal: He entered the jinshi examination and won renown.
translations.idiomatic: He sat for the jinshi degree and gained a name.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，廷試已落，復試，擢置高等，解褐歸德軍節度推官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he had failed the palace examination; on re-examination he was placed in the upper tier, and on leaving office was made judicial officer under the Guide de military commission.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 2 he had failed the palace exam; on a second sitting he ranked in the upper tier and entered service as judicial officer under the Guide de commission.

sentences.zh: 召還，授右拾遺、直史館。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed Right Remonstrator and duty scholar in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he became Right Remonstrator and duty scholar in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，通判壽、許二州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Duangong era he served as military prefect of Shou and Xu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Duangong he was military prefect of Shou and Xu.

sentences.zh: 歸宋，與左正言尹黃裳、馮拯、右正言王世則、宋沆伏閣請立許王元僖為儲貳，詞意狂率，太宗怒。

translations.literal: After returning to Song, together with Left Remonstrator Yin Huangshang, Feng Zheng, Right Remonstrator Wang Shize, and Song Hang, he knelt at the palace gate to request that Prince Xu, Yuanxi, be established as heir apparent; the language was rash and reckless, and the Taizong emperor was enraged.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to Song, he joined Left Remonstrator Yin Huangshang, Feng Zheng, Right Remonstrator Wang Shize, and Song Hang in kneeling at the palace gate to ask that Prince Xu, Yuanxi, be named heir apparent. Their language was reckless, and Taizong flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 時沆坐呂蒙正親黨，已出為宜州團練副使。

translations.literal: At the time Hang, as a partisan of Lü Mengzheng, had already been sent out as deputy militia commissioner of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hang, already banished as a partisan of Lü Mengzheng, was then deputy militia commissioner of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 上因語近臣曰：「儲副，邦國之本，朕豈不知。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore said to his close ministers: "The heir apparent is the root of the state—do I not know this?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then told his inner circle: "The heir apparent is the foundation of the realm—do you think I do not know it?

sentences.zh: 但近世淺薄，若立太子，即東宮僚屬皆須稱臣，官職聯次與上台無異，人情深所不安。

translations.literal: But in recent times people are shallow; if a crown prince is established, all Eastern Palace staff must address him as lord, and their ranks and titles follow in sequence no differently from those at the upper court—something men deeply find unsettling.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the age has grown shallow. Once a crown prince is named, every official in the Eastern Palace must call him lord, and their ranks stand in the same order as at court—a thing that deeply unsettles people.

sentences.zh: 此事朕自有時爾。」

translations.literal: On this matter I myself will act when the time comes."
translations.idiomatic: When the moment is right, I shall decide this myself.

sentences.zh: 湛坐削職，出知容州，黃裳知邕州，拯知端州，沆知靖州，世則知蒙州。

translations.literal: Zhan was stripped of office and sent out as prefect of Rongzhou; Huangshang was made prefect of Yongzhou, Zheng of Duanzhou, Hang of Jingzhou, and Shize of Mengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was demoted and sent to govern Rongzhou; Huangshang went to Yongzhou, Zheng to Duanzhou, Hang to Jingzhou, and Shize to Mengzhou.

sentences.zh: 容之戍卒謀竊發者，湛偵知，亟斬之。

translations.literal: Among the garrison soldiers at Rong there were some plotting a mutiny; Zhan detected it and swiftly executed them.
translations.idiomatic: At Rong, garrison troops were plotting a rising; Zhan learned of it and had them beheaded at once.

sentences.zh: 再遷比部員外郎，知郴、舒二州。

translations.literal: After two promotions he was Outer-Director in the Ministry of Revenue and prefect of Chen and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Two promotions later he was Outer-Director in the Ministry of Revenue and prefect in turn of Chen and Shu.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年召還，命試舍人院，復直史館。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he was recalled, ordered to take the drafting examination in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and restored as duty scholar in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 2 he was recalled, examined in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, and restored as duty scholar in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 是秋，命與閣門祗候韓紹輝使荊湖按視民事，條奏利病甚眾。

translations.literal: That autumn he was ordered with Palace Gate Commissioner Han Shaohui to inspect the Jing-Hu region and review the people's affairs; he submitted many memorials on benefits and harms.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he and Palace Gate Commissioner Han Shaohui were sent to inspect Jing-Hu and review local conditions; he memorialized extensively on what helped and harmed the people.

sentences.zh: 還，判三司都磨勘司。

translations.literal: On returning he was assigned to the Three Departments' central audit office.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was placed in charge of the Three Departments' central audit office.

sentences.zh: 又與王欽若同知貢舉，未幾，同修起居注。

translations.literal: He also served with Wang Qinruo as co-examiner for the metropolitan degree; before long he was appointed co-compiler of the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: He also joined Wang Qinruo as co-examiner for the metropolitan degree, and soon afterward became co-compiler of the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 時議城綏州，邊臣互言利害，遣湛與閣門祗候程順奇同往按視，湛言城之利有七而害有二，遂詔營葺，終以勞人罷之。

translations.literal: At the time there was debate over building a fort at Suizhou; frontier officials disputed the costs and benefits. Zhan was sent with Palace Gate Commissioner Cheng Shunqi to inspect on the spot. Zhan argued that building offered seven gains against two harms, and an edict ordered construction; in the end it was abandoned because it overtaxed the people.
translations.idiomatic: When officials debated fortifying Suizhou, border commanders disputed the trade-offs. Zhan and Palace Gate Commissioner Cheng Shunqi were dispatched to inspect. Zhan argued seven advantages against two drawbacks; construction was ordered, but in the end the work was dropped as too burdensome on the people.

sentences.zh: 湛美風儀，俊辯有材幹，凡五使西北議邊要。

translations.literal: Zhan had a fine presence, was quick and eloquent, and possessed talent and capacity; altogether he went five times on missions to the northwest to discuss frontier strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome in bearing, sharp of tongue, and capable in counsel, Zhan went five times to the northwest on missions concerning border strategy.

sentences.zh: 真宗有意擢任，顧遇甚厚。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong intended to promote him and treated him with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong meant to elevate him and showed him exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 曲宴苑中，賦賞花詩，不移晷以獻，深被褒賞。

translations.literal: At a private banquet in the park he composed a flower-appreciation poem and presented it before the shadow moved on the sundial; he received deep praise.
translations.idiomatic: At an informal garden banquet he wrote a flower-appreciation poem and submitted it before the sun had moved a fraction on the dial; the emperor praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 五年春，有河陰民常德方訟臨津尉任懿納賄登第，事下御史臺，鞫得懿款云：「咸平二年，補太學生，寓僧仁雅舍，因仁雅求院之主僧惠秦為道地，署紙許銀七鋌，仁雅、惠秦隱其二，易為五鋌。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, a He yin commoner named Chang Defang sued the Linjin district captain Ren Yi for taking bribes to pass the examinations. The case went to the Censorate; under interrogation Yi confessed: "In the second year of Xianping I entered the Imperial College as a supplemental student and lodged at the monk Renya's quarters. Through Renya I asked the college's chief monk Huiqin to pull strings and signed a note promising seven ingots of silver. Renya and Huiqin kept two for themselves and changed the amount to five.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the fifth year, a He yin commoner named Chang Defang accused Linjin district captain Ren Yi of buying his pass on the examinations. The Censorate took the case; under questioning Yi confessed: "In Xianping 2 I entered the Imperial College as a supplemental student and stayed at Monk Renya's lodgings. Through Renya I asked Chief Monk Huiqin of the college for favor and signed a note for seven ingots of silver. Renya and Huiqin kept two and altered the figure to five.

sentences.zh: 惠秦素識王欽若已在貢院，乃因館客寧文德、仆夫徐興納署紙於欽若妻李，李密召家仆祁睿書懿名於左臂，並口傳許賂之數，入省告欽若。

translations.literal: Huiqin already knew Wang Qinruo was in the examination hall; through the lodger Ning Wende and the servant Xu Xing he passed the signed note to Qinruo's wife Li. Li secretly summoned the household servant Qi Rui, had him write Yi's name on his left arm, and orally relayed the promised bribe; he entered the hall and informed Qinruo.
translations.idiomatic: Huiqin knew Wang Qinruo was already in the examination hall. Through the lodger Ning Wende and the servant Xu Xing he delivered the signed note to Qinruo's wife Li. Li secretly called the house servant Qi Rui, had Yi's name written on his left arm, and told him the promised sum by word of mouth; he entered the hall and reported to Qinruo.

sentences.zh: 及懿過五場，睿復持湯飲至省，欽若遣睿語李，令取其銀，懿未即與。

translations.literal: After Yi passed the fifth session, Rui again brought soup to the hall; Qinruo sent Rui to tell Li to collect the silver, but Yi did not immediately pay.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi had passed the fifth session, Rui once more brought soup to the hall. Qinruo sent him to tell Li to collect the silver, but Yi did not pay at once.

sentences.zh: 既而懿預奏名授官，未行，丁內艱，還鄉里。

translations.literal: Later Yi was listed among those passed and granted office, but before taking up his post he entered mourning for his mother and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was later placed on the pass list and granted an appointment, but before assuming office he went into mourning for his mother and returned home.

sentences.zh: 仁雅馳書索銀，形於詛罵。」

translations.literal: Renya sent a hurried letter demanding the silver, cursing and reviling in the open."
translations.idiomatic: Renya wrote demanding the silver in urgent, abusive terms.

sentences.zh: 德方者，賣卜縣市，獲其書，以告中丞趙昌言，具其事奏白，請逮欽若屬吏。

translations.literal: Defang, who told fortunes in the county market, obtained the letter and reported the whole affair to Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhao Changyan, who memorialized requesting that Qinruo be taken into custody as an official.
translations.idiomatic: Defang, a fortune-teller in the county market, got hold of the letter, laid the matter before Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhao Changyan, and memorialized asking that Qinruo be seized as a serving official.

sentences.zh: 先是，欽若為亳州判官，睿其廳幹，及代歸，以睿從行而未除州之役籍。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Qinruo had been a judicial officer in Bozhou, Rui was a clerk in his office; when Qinruo left and returned home he took Rui with him but never removed Rui's name from the prefecture's corvée register.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when Qinruo was judicial officer in Bozhou, Rui had been a clerk in his office. On leaving his post Qinruo took Rui home but never struck Rui's name from the prefecture corvée rolls.

sentences.zh: 及貢舉事畢，會州人張續還鄉行服，托為睿去籍名。

translations.literal: When the examination affair was finished, a Bozhou man named Zhang Xu returned home to observe mourning and was asked to remove Rui's name from the register.
translations.idiomatic: After the examination business was done, a Bozhou man named Zhang Xu went home to observe mourning and was entrusted to strike Rui's name from the register.

sentences.zh: 至是，欽若訴云：「睿休役之後，始傭於家，而惠秦未嘗及門。」

translations.literal: At this point Qinruo appealed, saying: "After Rui finished his corvée term he was only then hired into our household, and Huiqin never once came to our door."
translations.idiomatic: By then Qinruo filed an appeal, saying: "After Rui completed his corvée service he was only then taken on as a household servant, and Huiqin had never once set foot at our door."

sentences.zh: 欽若方被寵顧，乃詔翰林侍讀學士邢昺、內侍副都知閻承翰並驛召知曹州邊肅、知許州毋賓古就太常寺別鞫，懿易款云：「有妻兄張駕舉進士，識湛，懿亦與駕同造湛門，嘗以石榴二百枚、木炭百秤饋之。

translations.literal: Qinruo was then in imperial favor; an edict ordered Hanlin Academician Reader Xing Bing and Inner Service Deputy Director Yan Chenghan, by post relay, to summon Bian Su, prefect of Cao, and Wu Binggu, prefect of Xu, to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for separate interrogation. Yi changed his confession, saying: "My wife's elder brother Zhang Jia took the jinshi examination and knew Zhan; Yi also went with Jia to Zhan's door and once presented two hundred pomegranates and a hundred piculs of charcoal as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Qinruo was then in high favor at court. An edict ordered Hanlin Academician Reader Xing Bing and Inner Service Deputy Director Yan Chenghan to summon by post relay Bian Su, prefect of Cao, and Wu Binggu, prefect of Xu, to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for separate hearings. Yi revised his confession: "My wife's elder brother Zhang Jia had taken the jinshi examination and knew Zhan; Yi too had gone with Jia to Zhan's door and once sent two hundred pomegranates and a hundred piculs of charcoal as gifts.

sentences.zh: 懿之輸銀也，但憑二僧達一主司，實不知誰何？」

translations.literal: When Yi paid the silver, he relied only on the two monks to reach one chief examiner; he truly did not know who it was."
translations.idiomatic: When Yi paid the silver, he relied only on the two monks to reach one chief examiner and truly did not know who it was."

sentences.zh: 乃以為湛納其銀。

translations.literal: It was therefore concluded that Zhan had taken the silver.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was therefore held to have accepted the silver.

sentences.zh: 湛適使陝西，中途召還，時張駕已死，寧文德、徐興悉遁去，欽若近參機務，門下仆使多新募至，不識惠秦，故無與左證。

translations.literal: Zhan happened to be on mission in Shaanxi and was recalled midway. By then Zhang Jia was already dead; Ning Wende and Xu Xing had all fled. Qinruo was then close to the inner councils of state, and most of the servants at his gate were newly hired and did not know Huiqin, so there was no corroborating witness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was then on mission in Shaanxi and was recalled en route. Zhang Jia was already dead; Ning Wende and Xu Xing had all fled. Qinruo was then deeply involved in confidential affairs of state, and most servants at his gate were newly hired and did not know Huiqin, so no corroborating witness could be found.

sentences.zh: 又固執知舉時未有祁睿，遂以湛受銀，法當死，特詔削籍、流儋州。

translations.literal: They also insisted that when the examinations were conducted Qi Rui did not yet exist; thus Zhan was held to have taken silver, and by law deserved death, but a special edict stripped his registry and exiled him to Danzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Investigators also insisted that Qi Rui had not existed when the examinations were held; Zhan was therefore convicted of taking silver, which by law merited death, but a special edict stripped him from the rolls and exiled him to Danzhou.

sentences.zh: 懿杖脊、配隸忠靖軍。

translations.literal: Yi was beaten on the back and assigned to the Loyal Tranquility Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was flogged on the back and assigned to the Loyal Tranquility Army.

sentences.zh: 惠秦坐受簡劄及隱銀未入已，以年七十餘，當贖銅八斤，特杖一百，黥麵配商州坑冶。

translations.literal: Huiqin was punished for receiving the signed note and concealing silver not yet paid in; at over seventy years of age he should have redeemed the offense with eight jin of copper, but by special order he received a hundred blows, was tattooed on the face, and was assigned to the Shangzhou mining works.
translations.idiomatic: Huiqin was punished for receiving the signed note and for concealing silver not yet delivered. At over seventy he should have redeemed the offense with eight jin of copper, but by special order he received a hundred blows, was tattooed on the face, and was sent to the Shangzhou mining works.

sentences.zh: 仁雅杖脊，配隸郢州牢城，而不窮用銀之端。

translations.literal: Renya was beaten on the back and assigned to the Yingzhou garrison prison, and the trail of the silver was not pursued to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Renya was flogged on the back and assigned to the Yingzhou garrison prison, while the full trail of the silver was never pursued.

sentences.zh: 初，王旦與欽若知舉，出拜樞密副使，以湛代領其事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Dan and Qinruo had served as chief examiners; when Dan left to take the post of Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Zhan was appointed to succeed him in that duty.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Dan and Qinruo had served as chief examiners. When Dan left to become Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Zhan was appointed to succeed him as chief examiner.

sentences.zh: 湛之入貢院，懿已試第三場畢，及官收湛贓，家實無物。

translations.literal: When Zhan entered the examination hall, Yi had already finished the third session; when officials seized Zhan's bribe goods, his household in fact had nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhan entered the examination hall, Yi had already completed the third session. When officials searched for Zhan's bribe goods, his household in fact possessed nothing.

sentences.zh: 湛素與梁顥善，或假顥白金器，乃取以輸官。

translations.literal: Zhan had long been on good terms with Liang Hao; he borrowed Hao's white-gold vessels and then turned them in to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan had long been friendly with Liang Hao; he borrowed Hao's white-gold vessels and then surrendered them to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 六年，會赦移惠州，至化州調馬驛卒，年四十一。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when an amnesty moved him to Huizhou, he died at the Huazhou post station while requisitioning horses at the age of forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when an amnesty transferred him to Huizhou, he died at the Huazhou post station while requisitioning horses. He was forty-one.

sentences.zh: 湛時一子偕行，甚幼，州以聞，特詔賜錢二萬，官為護喪還揚州。

translations.literal: Zhan had one son traveling with him, very young; the prefecture reported this, and a special edict granted twenty thousand cash and ordered officials to escort the coffin back to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan had a very young son with him on the journey. The prefecture reported this, and a special edict granted twenty thousand cash and ordered officials to escort the coffin back to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 因詔命官配流嶺外而沒者，悉給緡錢，聽其歸葬，如親屬幼稚者，所在遣牙校部送之。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued that officials exiled beyond the Lingnan who died in exile should all be granted cash and allowed to return home for burial; where relatives were young and helpless, local officials were to dispatch clerks to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then provided that officials exiled beyond the Lingnan who died in exile should all receive cash and be allowed to return home for burial; where relatives were young and helpless, local officials were to dispatch clerks to escort them.

sentences.zh: 湛有集十卷。

translations.literal: Zhan left a collected works in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan left collected works in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子鼎，大中祥符四年進士，至度支員外郎、直史館、鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: His son Ding passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu and rose to Outer-Director in the Ministry of Revenue, duty scholar in the Historiography Institute, and Salt and Iron Commission judge.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ding passed the jinshi examination in Dazhong Xiangfu 4 and rose to Outer-Director in the Ministry of Revenue, duty scholar in the Historiography Institute, and Salt and Iron Commission judge.

sentences.zh: 路振，字子發，永州祁陽人，唐相岩之四世孫。

translations.literal: Lu Zhen, courtesy name Zifa, was a native of Qiyang in Yongzhou and the fourth-generation descendant of the Tang chancellor Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhen, courtesy name Zifa, was a native of Qiyang in Yongzhou and a fourth-generation descendant of the Tang chancellor Yan.

sentences.zh: 岩貶死嶺外，其子琛避地湖湘間，遂居焉。

translations.literal: Yan was demoted and died beyond the Lingnan; his son Chen took refuge in the lakes and rivers of Hunan and settled there.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was demoted and died in exile beyond the Lingnan; his son Chen took refuge in the lake country of Hunan and settled there.

sentences.zh: 振父洵美事馬希杲，署連州從事，謝病終於家。

translations.literal: Zhen's father Xunmei served Ma Xiguo and was appointed an aide in Lianzhou; he resigned on grounds of illness and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's father Xunmei served Ma Xiguo, was appointed an aide in Lianzhou, resigned on grounds of illness, and died at home.

sentences.zh: 振幼穎悟，五歲誦《孝經》、《論語》。

translations.literal: Zhen was bright from childhood; at five he could recite the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was precocious as a child; at five he could recite the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.

sentences.zh: 十歲聽講《陰符》，裁百言而止，洵美責之，俾終其業。

translations.literal: At ten he listened to lectures on the Yin Convergence Classic and stopped after only a hundred words; Xunmei rebuked him and made him finish the study.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he listened to lectures on the Yin Convergence Classic and stopped after only a hundred words. Xunmei rebuked him and made him complete the study.

sentences.zh: 振曰：「百言演道足矣，餘何必學？」

translations.literal: Zhen said: "A hundred words are enough to expound the Way; why must one learn the rest?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said: "A hundred words suffice to expound the Way—why learn the rest?"

sentences.zh: 洵美大奇之。

translations.literal: Xunmei was greatly astonished by him.
translations.idiomatic: Xunmei was deeply astonished.

sentences.zh: 十二丁外艱，母氏慮其廢業，日加誨激，雖隆冬盛署，未始有懈。

translations.literal: At twelve he entered mourning for his father; his mother feared he would abandon his studies and daily urged and spurred him on, so that even in deep winter or blazing summer he never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he entered mourning for his father. His mother feared he would abandon his studies and daily urged him on, so that even in deep winter or blazing summer he never slackened.

sentences.zh: 淳化中舉進士，太宗以詞場之弊，多事輕淺，不能該貫古道，因試《卮言日出賦》，觀其學術。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era he passed the jinshi examination. Because the abuses of the examination halls lay in treating too many trivial and shallow topics and failing to embrace the full ancient Way, Taizong set the theme "The Goblet Speaks: The Sun Rises," to observe the candidates' learning.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chunhua era he passed the jinshi examination. Taizong, finding examination essays too often trivial and shallow and unable to embrace the full ancient Way, set the theme "The Goblet Speaks: The Sun Rises" to test the candidates' learning.

sentences.zh: 時就試者凡數百人，咸咢眙忘其所出，雖當時馳聲場屋者亦有難色。

translations.literal: At the time several hundred candidates were taking the examination; all gaped in astonishment and forgot what they were writing, and even those then famous in the halls of examination showed difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred candidates were taking the examination; all stared in astonishment and forgot what they were writing, and even those then famous in the examination halls showed distress.

sentences.zh: 振寒素，遊京師人罕知者，所作賦尤為典贍，太宗甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Zhen was poor and plain; few in the capital knew him, yet the fu he wrote was especially classical and ample, and Taizong greatly praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was poor and obscure; few in the capital knew him, yet his fu was especially classical and ample, and Taizong greatly praised it.

sentences.zh: 擢置甲科，釋褐大理評事，通判邠州，徙徐州。

translations.literal: He was placed in the top grade, entered service as an appraiser in the Court of Judicial Review, served as administrative coordinator of Bin Prefecture, and was transferred to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was placed in the top grade, entered service as an appraiser in the Court of Judicial Review, served as administrative coordinator of Bin Prefecture, and was transferred to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 召還，直史館，復遣之任，遷太子中允、知濱州。

translations.literal: Recalled to court, he served as duty scholar in the Historiography Institute, was sent back to his post, and was promoted to Vice Director in the Crown Prince's Household and prefect of Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he served as duty scholar in the Historiography Institute, was sent back to his post, and was promoted to Vice Director in the Crown Prince's Household and prefect of Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 一日，契丹至城下，兵少，民相恐，眾謂振文吏，無戰禦方略，環聚而泣。

translations.literal: One day the Khitan reached the city walls; the garrison was small and the people were afraid. The crowd said Zhen was a civil official with no strategy for battle or defense, and they gathered in a ring weeping.
translations.idiomatic: One day the Khitan reached the city walls. The garrison was small and the people were terrified. The crowd said Zhen was a civil official with no strategy for battle or defense, and they gathered weeping.

sentences.zh: 振乃親加撫諭，且以敵盛不可與爭鋒，宜堅壁自守。

translations.literal: Zhen then personally went among them to reassure them, saying that the enemy was strong and could not be met in open battle, and that they should hold the walls and defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen then went among them in person to reassure them, saying the enemy was too strong to meet in open battle and that they should hold the walls and defend themselves.

sentences.zh: 數日，契丹引去。

translations.literal: After several days the Khitan withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After several days the Khitan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 轉運使劉綜稱其能，詔書褒美。

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Liu Zong praised his competence, and an edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Liu Zong praised his competence, and an edict commended him.

sentences.zh: 常作《祭戰馬文》曰：

translations.literal: He once composed an "Elegy for War Horses," which reads:
translations.idiomatic: He once composed an "Elegy for War Horses," which reads:

sentences.zh: 咸平中，契丹犯高陽關，執大將康保裔，略河朔而去。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era the Khitan violated Gaoyang Pass, captured the great general Kang Baoyi, and plundered the Hebei region before withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianping era the Khitan breached Gaoyang Pass, captured the great general Kang Baoyi, and plundered the Hebei region before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 天子幸魏，特遣將王榮以五千騎追之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven went in person to Wei and specially dispatched the general Wang Rong with five thousand cavalry to pursue them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went in person to Wei and specially dispatched General Wang Rong with five thousand cavalry in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 榮無將材，但能走馬，以馳射為事，受命恇怯，數日不敢行，伺賊渡河而後發。

translations.literal: Rong had no talent as a commander; he could only ride fast and made mounted archery his occupation. When he received the order he was timid and for several days did not dare advance, waiting until the bandits had crossed the river before setting out.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had no talent as a commander; he could only ride fast and made mounted archery his occupation. When he received the order he was timid and for several days did not dare advance, waiting until the enemy had crossed the river before setting out.

sentences.zh: 有剽淄、齊者數千騎尚屯泥沽，榮不欲見敵，遂以其騎略河南岸而還。

translations.literal: Several thousand cavalry raiding from Zi and Qi were still encamped at Nigu, but Rong did not wish to meet the enemy and instead led his horsemen to raid the south bank of the Yellow River before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand cavalry raiding from Zi and Qi were still encamped at Nigu, but Rong did not wish to meet the enemy and instead led his horsemen to raid the south bank of the Yellow River before returning.

sentences.zh: 晝夜急騎，馬不秣而道斃者十有四五，天子憫之，遣使收瘞焉。

translations.literal: They rode hard day and night; the horses were not fed, and ten or fifteen in every hundred died on the road. The Son of Heaven took pity on them and sent envoys to gather and bury them.
translations.idiomatic: They rode hard day and night without feeding the horses, and ten or fifteen in every hundred died on the road. The emperor took pity on them and sent envoys to gather and bury them.

sentences.zh: 因作祭文曰：

translations.literal: He therefore composed an elegy, which reads:
translations.idiomatic: He therefore composed an elegy, which reads:

sentences.zh: 房駟之精，降為驪騂。

translations.literal: The essence of the Fang-star steeds descended and became bay and chestnut horses.
translations.idiomatic: The essence of the Fang-star steeds descended and became bay and chestnut horses.

sentences.zh: 飲泉呀風，流沙激霆。

translations.literal: They drank at springs and snorted at the wind; sand flowed like streams and thunder was stirred.
translations.idiomatic: They drank at springs and snorted into the wind; desert sand surged like streams and thunder was stirred.

sentences.zh: 虎脊孤聳，龍媒鷙獰。

translations.literal: Tiger spines rose alone; dragon sires stared fierce and grim.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger backs rose alone; dragon sires stared fierce and grim.

sentences.zh: 丹髦曉霞，的顙秋星。

translations.literal: Crimson manes were like dawn clouds; white foreheads like autumn stars.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson manes were like dawn clouds; white foreheads like autumn stars.

sentences.zh: 茀方著幹，宜乘旋膺。

translations.literal: Square patterns marked their withers; fit to ride, they turned their chests.
translations.idiomatic: Square patterns marked their withers; fit to ride, they turned their chests upward.

sentences.zh: 巉臚角起，方背珠明。

translations.literal: High foreheads and horns rose up; square backs gleamed like pearls.
translations.idiomatic: High foreheads and horns rose up; square backs gleamed like pearls.

sentences.zh: 爾其絕塞草荒，八月隕霜。

translations.literal: You crossed the frontier wastes where grass ran wild; in the eighth month frost fell.
translations.idiomatic: You crossed the frontier wastes where grass ran wild; in the eighth month frost fell.

sentences.zh: 毛縮蹄堅，筋舒脈張。

translations.literal: Coats drew tight and hooves hardened; sinews loosened and veins spread wide.
translations.idiomatic: Coats drew tight and hooves hardened; sinews loosened and veins spread wide.

sentences.zh: 獸惡恐噬，虯獰欲驤。

translations.literal: Beasts snarled in fear of biting; horned dragons reared, eager to gallop.
translations.idiomatic: Beasts snarled in fear of biting; horned dragons reared, eager to gallop.

sentences.zh: 噴沙散沫，千里飛雪。

translations.literal: They sprayed sand and scattered foam; for a thousand li snow seemed to fly.
translations.idiomatic: They sprayed sand and scattered foam; for a thousand li snow seemed to fly.

sentences.zh: 圉人負紖，武士索鐵。

translations.literal: Grooms bore the leading ropes; warriors sought the iron bits.
translations.idiomatic: Grooms bore the leading ropes; warriors sought the iron bits.

sentences.zh: 前遮後突，雷動地裂。

translations.literal: Blocked in front and charged from behind, they thundered and split the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Blocked in front and charged from behind, they thundered and split the earth.

sentences.zh: 急挽一而製百，終伏撾而受絏。

translations.literal: Pulling one rein to control a hundred, in the end they bowed to the whip and accepted the halter.
translations.idiomatic: Pulling one rein to control a hundred, in the end they bowed to the whip and accepted the halter.

sentences.zh: 牧官劬劬，歲入券書。

translations.literal: Pasture officials toiled diligently; each year they entered tally records.
translations.idiomatic: Pasture officials toiled diligently; each year they entered tally records.

sentences.zh: 蹄钜累累，通乎鬼區。

translations.literal: Great hoofprints piled up one upon another, reaching into the demon lands.
translations.idiomatic: Great hoofprints piled up one upon another, reaching into the demon lands.

sentences.zh: 名駒大𩡺，銜尾入塞。

translations.literal: Famous colts and great steeds entered the frontier pass tail to tail.
translations.idiomatic: Famous colts and great steeds entered the frontier pass tail to tail.

sentences.zh: 勞其酋長，節以駔儈。

translations.literal: Their chieftains were wearied; horse brokers were sent to regulate them.
translations.idiomatic: Their chieftains were wearied; horse brokers were sent to regulate them.

sentences.zh: 蜀錦吳繒，積如丘陵。

translations.literal: Shu brocades and Wu silks piled up like hills and mounds.
translations.idiomatic: Shu brocades and Wu silks piled up like hills and mounds.

sentences.zh: 馬歸於我也重，幣入於彼也輕。

translations.literal: Horses returning to us were heavy in cost; tribute goods entering them were light.
translations.idiomatic: Horses returning to us were heavy in cost; tribute goods entering them were light.

sentences.zh: 於是絡黃金之羈，浴天池之波。

translations.literal: Then they were bound with golden bridles and bathed in the waves of the Heavenly Pool.
translations.idiomatic: Then they were bound with golden bridles and bathed in the waves of the Heavenly Pool.

sentences.zh: 鼓鬛雲衢，弄影星河。

translations.literal: They shook their manes on the cloud roads and cast their shadows among the stars and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: They shook their manes on the cloud roads and cast their shadows among the stars and rivers.

sentences.zh: 或踶而齧，或嗅而吪。

translations.literal: Some kicked and bit; some sniffed and whinnied.
translations.idiomatic: Some kicked and bit; some sniffed and whinnied.

sentences.zh: 原蠶申禁，駔駿何多。

translations.literal: Silkworms on the plain were forbidden by edict; yet how many fine steeds were there?
translations.idiomatic: Silkworms on the plain were forbidden by edict; yet how many fine steeds were there?

sentences.zh: 帝念神物，來經遠道。

translations.literal: The emperor thought on these divine creatures, come from distant roads.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought on these divine creatures, come from distant roads.

sentences.zh: 閱之於內殿，養之於外皂，飲以玉池，秣之瑤草。

translations.literal: He reviewed them in the inner hall, kept them in the outer stable, gave them jade pools to drink from, and fed them jade grass.
translations.idiomatic: He reviewed them in the inner hall, kept them in the outer stable, gave them jade pools to drink from, and fed them jade grass.

sentences.zh: 窮冬邊塵，入我河漘。

translations.literal: At the bitter end of winter frontier dust rose and entered our river banks.
translations.idiomatic: At the bitter end of winter frontier dust rose and entered our river banks.

sentences.zh: 羽書宵飛，龍馭北巡。

translations.literal: Feathered dispatches flew by night; the dragon chariot toured north.
translations.idiomatic: Feathered dispatches flew by night; the dragon chariot toured north.

sentences.zh: 選仗下之名馬，屬閫外之武臣。

translations.literal: Famous horses from the imperial stables were chosen and entrusted to military officers beyond the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Famous horses from the imperial stables were chosen and entrusted to military officers beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 周戈電燭，禁旅星陳。

translations.literal: Zhou halberds flashed like lightning; palace guards stood starlike in array.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou halberds flashed like lightning; palace guards stood starlike in array.

sentences.zh: 授以長策，帥以全軍。

translations.literal: They were given long whips and put in command of the full army.
translations.idiomatic: They were given long whips and put in command of the full army.

sentences.zh: 壯士怒兮山可擘，猛馬哮兮虎可咋。

translations.literal: Brave men were angry enough to split mountains; fierce horses roared as though tigers could be seized.
translations.idiomatic: Brave men were angry enough to split mountains; fierce horses roared as though tigers could be seized.

sentences.zh: 何嚄唶之無勇，反遷延而避敵。

translations.literal: Why were they clamorous yet without courage, instead delaying and avoiding the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: Why were they clamorous yet without courage, instead delaying and avoiding the enemy?

sentences.zh: 冰霜淒淒，介甲而馳。

translations.literal: Frost and ice were bitter cold; clad in armor they galloped on.
translations.idiomatic: Frost and ice were bitter cold; clad in armor they galloped on.

sentences.zh: 不飲不秣，載渴載饑。

translations.literal: They neither drank nor were fed; they bore thirst and hunger together.
translations.idiomatic: They neither drank nor were fed; they bore thirst and hunger together.

sentences.zh: 駿馬餒死，行人嗟谘。

translations.literal: Fine horses starved to death; travelers sighed and lamented.
translations.idiomatic: Fine horses starved to death; travelers sighed and lamented.

sentences.zh: 委天骨於衢路，反星精於雲霧。

translations.literal: Heaven-born bones were cast upon the highway; star essence returned to cloud and mist.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven-born bones were cast upon the highway; star essence returned to cloud and mist.

sentences.zh: 報主恩之無及，齊戎力而何誤。

translations.literal: Repaying the lord's grace was no longer possible; matching military strength—where was the error?
translations.idiomatic: Repaying the lord's grace was no longer possible; matching military strength—where lay the error?

sentences.zh: 生芻致祭，弊帷成禮。

translations.literal: Fresh fodder was offered in sacrifice; worn curtains became the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh fodder was offered in sacrifice; worn curtains became the rites.

sentences.zh: 瘞於崇岡，全爾具體。

translations.literal: Buried on a lofty hill, may your whole body be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Buried on a lofty hill, may your whole body be preserved.

sentences.zh: 馬如有神，知帝之仁。

translations.literal: If horses have spirit, they know the emperor's benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: If horses have spirit, they know the emperor's benevolence.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 又以西兵未弭，入判大理寺，改太常丞、知河中府，徙知鄧州。

translations.literal: Because western campaigns had not yet been settled, he entered to serve as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, was changed to Assistant Director in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Hezhong, and was transferred to be prefect of Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because western campaigns had not yet been settled, he entered to serve as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, was changed to Assistant Director in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Hezhong, and was transferred to be prefect of Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 代還，判吏部南曹三司催欠憑由司。

translations.literal: When his replacement returned, he served as vice director of the Ministry of Personnel's Southern Bureau and of the Three Departments' voucher office for pressing overdue accounts.
translations.idiomatic: When his replacement returned, he served as vice director of the Ministry of Personnel's Southern Bureau and of the Three Departments' voucher office for pressing overdue accounts.

sentences.zh: 景德中使福建巡撫，俄判鼓司登聞院。

translations.literal: In the Jingde era he was sent to inspect Fujian; soon afterward he served as vice director of the Drum Office and Petition Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingde era he was sent to inspect Fujian; soon afterward he served as vice director of the Drum Office and Petition Court.

sentences.zh: 會修《兩朝國史》，以振為編修官。

translations.literal: When the Two-Reigns National History was being compiled, Zhen was appointed a compiling editor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Two-Reigns National History was being compiled, Zhen was appointed a compiling editor.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，使契丹，撰《乘軺錄》以獻。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he was sent as envoy to the Khitan and presented his Record of a Carriage Journey.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he was sent as envoy to the Khitan and presented his Record of a Carriage Journey.

sentences.zh: 改太常博士、左司諫，擢知制誥。

translations.literal: He was changed to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Left Remonstrance Officer, and was promoted to drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Left Remonstrance Officer, and was promoted to drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 振文詞溫麗，屢奏賦頌，為名輩所稱，尤長詩詠，多警句。

translations.literal: Zhen's literary style was warm and elegant; he repeatedly submitted fu and eulogies and was praised by leading figures, especially excelling in poetry, with many striking lines.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's literary style was warm and elegant; he repeatedly submitted fu and eulogies and was praised by leading figures, especially excelling in poetry, with many striking lines.

sentences.zh: 及居文翰之職，深愜物議，自是彌加精厲。

translations.literal: Once he took up a literary post he deeply satisfied public opinion, and from then on applied himself all the more diligently.
translations.idiomatic: Once he took up a literary post he deeply satisfied public opinion, and from then on applied himself all the more diligently.

sentences.zh: 從祀譙、亳，時同職分局掌事，振獨直行在，專典綸翰，箋奏填委，應用無滯，時推其敏贍。

translations.literal: When he followed the emperor in sacrifice at Qiao and Bo, his colleagues at the same post divided the duties, but Zhen alone remained at the temporary palace and exclusively managed drafting; memorials and reports piled up, yet he answered every demand without delay, and contemporaries praised his quickness and fullness of talent.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed the emperor in sacrifice at Qiao and Bo, his colleagues at the same post divided the duties, but Zhen alone remained at the temporary palace and exclusively managed drafting; memorials and reports piled up, yet he answered every demand without delay, and contemporaries praised his quickness and fullness of talent.

sentences.zh: 七年，同修起居注，張復、崔遵度以書事誤失降秩，擇振與夏竦代之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed co-compiler of the Veritable Records; Zhang Fu and Cui Zundu were reduced in rank for errors in recording affairs, and Zhen and Xia Song were chosen to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed co-compiler of the Veritable Records; Zhang Fu and Cui Zundu were reduced in rank for errors in recording affairs, and Zhen and Xia Song were chosen to replace them.

sentences.zh: 嗜酒得疾，其冬卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: He fell ill from heavy drinking and died that winter at the age of fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill from heavy drinking and died that winter at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 錄其子綸為太常寺奉禮郎。

translations.literal: His son Lun was recorded as a Ceremonial Officer in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lun was recorded as a Ceremonial Officer in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 振純厚無城府，恂恂如也，時人惜其登用之晚。

translations.literal: Zhen was pure, generous, and without hidden designs, always deferential and mild; men of the time regretted that he had been placed in office so late.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was pure, generous, and without hidden designs, always deferential and mild; men of the time regretted that he had been placed in office so late.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collection in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 又嘗采五代末九國君臣行事作世家、列傳，書未成而卒。

translations.literal: He also once gathered the deeds of rulers and ministers of the nine states at the end of the Five Dynasties to compose house histories and biographies, but the book was unfinished when he died.
translations.idiomatic: He also once gathered the deeds of rulers and ministers of the nine states at the end of the Five Dynasties to compose house histories and biographies, but the book was unfinished when he died.

sentences.zh: 崔遵度，字堅白，本江陵人，後徙淄州之淄川。

translations.literal: Cui Zundu, courtesy name Jianbai, was originally a native of Jiangling and later moved to Zichuan in Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zundu, courtesy name Jianbai, was originally a native of Jiangling and later moved to Zichuan in Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 純介好學，始七歲，授經於叔父憲，嘗以《春秋》編年、《史》、《漢》紀傳之例問於憲，憲曰：「此兒他日成令名矣。」

translations.literal: Pure, upright, and fond of learning, at only seven he received instruction from his uncle Xian and once asked Xian about the methods of the Spring and Autumn Annals in chronological form and of the Records and Han in annal-biography form.
