Xian said: "This boy will one day win a fine reputation."
translations.idiomatic: Pure, upright, and fond of learning, at only seven he received instruction from his uncle Xian and once asked Xian about the methods of the Spring and Autumn Annals in chronological form and of the Records and Han in annal-biography form. Xian said: "This boy will one day win a fine reputation."

sentences.zh: 太平興國八年舉進士，解褐和州主簿，換臨汾。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination, entered service as registrar of He Prefecture, and was transferred to Linfen.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 8 he passed the jinshi examination, entered service as registrar of He Prefecture, and was transferred to Linfen.

sentences.zh: 饋芻糧，三抵綏州，涉無定河，河沙與水混流無定跡，陷溺相繼，遵度憫之，著銘以紀焉。

translations.literal: He supplied fodder and grain, thrice reaching Suizhou, crossed the Wuding River—the river's sand and water mixed in flow with no fixed trace, drownings followed one after another. Zundu pitied this and composed an inscription to record it.
translations.idiomatic: He supplied fodder and grain, making three trips to Suizhou. Crossing the Wuding River—where sand and water mixed in a current with no fixed channel—men drowned one after another. Zundu was moved by this and wrote an inscription to commemorate the events.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，轉運副使夏侯濤上其勤狀，召歸，對便坐，因獻文自薦。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong, Assistant Transport Commissioner Xiahou Tao submitted a report of his diligence; he was summoned back, answered at an informal audience, and thereupon presented a literary piece recommending himself.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Duangong era, Assistant Transport Commissioner Xiahou Tao submitted a report praising Zundu's diligence. Zundu was summoned to court, received an informal audience, and took the occasion to present a literary work recommending himself.

sentences.zh: 時新建秘閣，命中書試作頌一首，擢著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At that time the Secret Pavilion was newly built; the court ordered the Secretariat to test him by composing one eulogy, and he was promoted to Assistant Editor in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: The Secret Pavilion had just been established, and the court ordered the Secretariat to test him by having him compose an eulogy. He was promoted to Assistant Editor in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，吏部侍郎李至薦之，遷殿中丞，出知忠州。

translations.literal: In the Chunhua era, Vice Minister of Personnel Li Zhi recommended him; he was moved to Palace Censor and sent out as prefect of Zhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua era, Vice Minister of Personnel Li Zhi recommended him. He was promoted to Palace Censor and appointed prefect of Zhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李順之亂，賊遣其黨張餘來攻，遵度領甲士百餘背城而戰，賊逾堞以入，遵度投江中，賴州兵援之，得免。

translations.literal: In the rebellion of Li Shun, the rebels sent their partisan Zhang Yu to attack; Zundu led more than a hundred armored soldiers to fight with their backs to the city wall; the rebels crossed the parapet to enter; Zundu threw himself into the river; relying on prefectural troops to rescue him, he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: During Li Shun's rebellion, the rebels sent their partisan Zhang Yu to attack. Zundu led more than a hundred armored soldiers in a desperate fight with their backs to the wall, but the rebels scaled the parapet and broke in. Zundu threw himself into the river and was saved thanks to the prefectural troops who came to his aid.

sentences.zh: 坐失城池，貶崇陽令，移鹿邑。

translations.literal: For losing the city and prefecture, he was demoted to magistrate of Chongyang and transferred to Luyi.
translations.idiomatic: For the loss of the city he was demoted to magistrate of Chongyang, then transferred to Luyi.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，復為太子中允。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping, he was again made Palace Writer to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xianping era, he was restored as Palace Writer to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 景德初，內出遵度名，引對崇政殿，詔索所著文，召試舍人院，改太常丞、直史館。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, Zundu's name was issued from within the palace; he was brought for audience in Chongzheng Hall; the edict requested his writings; he was summoned for examination at the Drafting Academy; he was changed to Assistant Director in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and compiler attached to the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingde era, the emperor issued Zundu's name from within the palace and summoned him for audience in Chongzheng Hall. An edict requested his writings, and he was tested at the Drafting Academy. He was appointed Assistant Director in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and a compiler attached to the History Office.

sentences.zh: 會修《兩朝國史》，與路振並為編修官。

translations.literal: When the Two-Reigns National History was being compiled, he and Lu Zhen were together appointed compiling editors.
translations.idiomatic: When the Two-Reigns National History was being compiled, he and Lu Zhen were appointed co-compiling editors.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，命同修起居注。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, he was ordered to co-compile the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, he was ordered to co-compile the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 東封，進博士，祀汾陰，是歲，真宗以兩省官絕少，故因覃慶選補之，命為左司諫。

translations.literal: At the Eastern Ascension Sacrifice, he was advanced to Erudite; at the sacrifice at Fenyin; that year, Emperor Zhenzong because officials of the Two Departments were extremely few, therefore on the occasion of extending a celebratory favor selected and filled vacancies, appointing him Left Remonstrance Officer.
translations.idiomatic: At the Eastern Ascension Sacrifice he was promoted to Erudite, and at the sacrifice at Fenyin. That year, because officials of the Two Departments were extremely scarce, Emperor Zhenzong took the occasion of a celebratory amnesty to fill vacancies and appointed Zundu Left Remonstrance Officer.

sentences.zh: 遵度與物無競，口不言是非，淳澹清素，於勢利泊如也。

translations.literal: Zundu did not contend with things, his mouth did not speak of right and wrong, pure and simple in clarity and austerity; toward power and profit he was utterly indifferent.
translations.idiomatic: Zundu did not contend with others, never spoke of right and wrong, and lived in pure, unadorned simplicity; toward power and profit he was utterly indifferent.

sentences.zh: 掌右史十餘歲，立殿墀上，常退匿楹間，慮上之見。

translations.literal: He managed the Right Historian's duties for more than ten years; standing on the hall terrace, he often withdrew and hid among the pillars, fearing that the sovereign would see him.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Right Historian for more than ten years. When standing on the hall terrace he often withdrew to hide among the pillars, fearing that the emperor would notice him.

sentences.zh: 善鼓琴，得其深趣。

translations.literal: He was skilled at playing the qin and grasped its profound delight.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at the qin and grasped its deepest meaning.

sentences.zh: 所僦舍甚湫隘，有小閣，手植竹數本，朝退，默坐其上，彈琴獨酌，翛然自適。

translations.literal: The rented dwelling was very damp and cramped; there was a small loft; he personally planted several stalks of bamboo; after retiring from court in the morning, he silently sat upon it, played the qin and drank alone, carefree and self-content.
translations.idiomatic: His rented dwelling was damp and cramped, but it had a small loft where he had planted several stalks of bamboo with his own hands. After court each morning he would sit there in silence, playing the qin and drinking alone in tranquil contentment.

sentences.zh: 嘗著《琴箋》云：

translations.literal: He once wrote Notes on the Qin, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote his Notes on the Qin, saying:

sentences.zh: 世之言琴者，必曰長三尺六寸象期之日，十三徽象期之月，居中者象閏，前世未有辨者。

translations.literal: Those who speak of the qin in the world invariably say that its length of three chi and six cun symbolizes the days of a year, its thirteen stopping positions symbolize the months of a year, and the center one symbolizes the intercalary month—none in former ages had clarified this.
translations.idiomatic: Those who discuss the qin invariably say that its length of three chi and six cun represents the days of a year, its thirteen stopping positions represent the months, and the center position represents the intercalary month—yet no one in earlier ages had truly explained this.

sentences.zh: 至唐協律郎劉貺以樂器配諸節候，而謂琴為夏至之音。

translations.literal: By the Tang, the Harmony Officer Liu Kuang matched musical instruments to the seasonal divisions and held that the qin was the sound of the summer solstice.
translations.idiomatic: By the Tang dynasty, the Harmony Officer Liu Kuang matched musical instruments to the seasonal divisions and held that the qin was the sound of the summer solstice.

sentences.zh: 至於泛聲，卒無述者，愚嘗病之。

translations.literal: As for harmonics, in the end no one had explained them; I have long found this troubling.
translations.idiomatic: As for harmonics, no one had ever adequately explained them—a deficiency I have long lamented.

sentences.zh: 因張弓附案，泛其弦而十三徽聲具焉，況琴瑟之弦乎！

translations.literal: Therefore I stretched a bow against a table, touched harmonics on its string, and the sounds of all thirteen stopping positions were present—how much more so with the strings of qin and se!
translations.idiomatic: So I stretched a bow against a table, touched harmonics on its string, and all thirteen stopping positions sounded forth—how much more must this be true of the strings of qin and se!

sentences.zh: 是知非所謂象者，蓋天地自然之節耳，又豈止夏至之音而已。

translations.literal: From this one knows that what are called symbols are in fact the natural divisions of Heaven and Earth—not merely the sound of the summer solstice.
translations.idiomatic: From this one knows that what are called symbols are in fact the natural divisions of Heaven and Earth—and not merely the sound of the summer solstice alone.

sentences.zh: 夫《易》有太極，是生兩儀。

translations.literal: In the Changes there is the Supreme Pole; from it the Two Forms are generated.
translations.idiomatic: In the Changes there is the Supreme Pole, and from it the Two Forms are generated.

sentences.zh: 兩儀者，太極之節也；

translations.literal: The Two Forms are the divisions of the Supreme Pole;
translations.idiomatic: The Two Forms are the divisions of the Supreme Pole;

sentences.zh: 四時者，兩儀之節也；

translations.literal: the four seasons are the divisions of the Two Forms;
translations.idiomatic: the four seasons are the divisions of the Two Forms;

sentences.zh: 律呂者，四時之節也；

translations.literal: the pitch pipes are the divisions of the four seasons;
translations.idiomatic: the pitch pipes are the divisions of the four seasons;

sentences.zh: 晝夜者，律呂之節也；

translations.literal: day and night are the divisions of the pitch pipes;
translations.idiomatic: day and night are the divisions of the pitch pipes;

sentences.zh: 刻漏者，晝夜之節也。

translations.literal: the clepsydra marks are the divisions of day and night.
translations.idiomatic: the clepsydra marks are the divisions of day and night.

sentences.zh: 節節相交，自細至大而歲成焉。

translations.literal: Division intersects with division, from the fine to the great, and the year is completed.
translations.idiomatic: Each division intersects with the next, from the smallest to the greatest, until the year is complete.

sentences.zh: 既不可使之節，亦不可使之不節，氣之自然者也。

translations.literal: It cannot be made to divide, nor can it be made not to divide—this is the naturalness of qi.
translations.idiomatic: It cannot be forced to divide, nor can it be forced not to divide—such is the natural course of qi.

sentences.zh: 氣既節矣，聲同則應，既不可使之應，亦不可使之不應，數之自然者也。

translations.literal: Once qi has divided, sounds of the same kind respond; it cannot be made to respond, nor can it be made not to respond—this is the naturalness of number.
translations.idiomatic: Once qi has divided, like sounds respond to one another; response cannot be forced, nor can it be prevented—such is the natural course of number.

sentences.zh: 既節且應，則天地之文成矣。

translations.literal: Once there is both division and response, the pattern of Heaven and Earth is complete.
translations.idiomatic: When division and response are both present, the pattern of Heaven and Earth is complete.

sentences.zh: 文之義也，或任形而著，或假物而彰。

translations.literal: The meaning of pattern: sometimes it manifests through form, sometimes it is revealed through things.
translations.idiomatic: The meaning of pattern is this: sometimes it manifests through form, sometimes it is revealed through things.

sentences.zh: 日星文乎上，山川理乎下，動物植物，花者節者，五色具矣。

translations.literal: Sun and stars pattern the heavens above, mountains and rivers order the earth below; moving creatures and plants, flowers and seasonal growth—all five colors are present.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and stars pattern the heavens above, mountains and rivers order the earth below; among moving creatures and plants, flowers and seasonal growth—all five colors are present.

sentences.zh: 斯任形者也。

translations.literal: This is manifesting through form.
translations.idiomatic: This is manifesting through form.

sentences.zh: 至於人常有五性而不著，以事觀之然後著；

translations.literal: As for human beings, the five natures are always present but not visible; only when observed through affairs do they become visible;
translations.idiomatic: Human beings always possess the five natures, yet they are not visible; only when observed through conduct do they become manifest;

sentences.zh: 日常有五色而不見，以水觀之然後見；

translations.literal: the sun always has five colors but they are not seen; only when observed through water do they become seen;
translations.idiomatic: the sun always holds five colors, yet they cannot be seen; only when observed through water do they become visible;

sentences.zh: 氣常有五音而不聞，以弦考之然後聞。

translations.literal: qi always has the five tones but they are not heard; only when tested on strings do they become heard.
translations.idiomatic: qi always holds the five tones, yet they cannot be heard; only when tested on strings do they become audible.

sentences.zh: 斯假物者也。

translations.literal: This is revealing through things.
translations.idiomatic: This is revealing through things.

sentences.zh: 是故聖人不能作《易》而能知自然之數，不能作琴而能知自然之節。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage cannot compose the Changes yet can know the numbers of nature; cannot compose the qin yet can know the divisions of nature.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sage need not compose the Changes to know the numbers of nature, nor compose the qin to know the divisions of nature.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 數本於一而成於三，因而重之，故《易》六畫而成卦。

translations.literal: Number originates in one and is completed in three; then doubled again, therefore the Changes uses six lines to form a hexagram.
translations.idiomatic: Number originates in one and is completed in three; doubled again, the Changes uses six lines to form a hexagram.

sentences.zh: 及其應也，一必於四，二必於五，三必於六焉。

translations.literal: When they respond, one must be at four, two must be at five, three must be at six.
translations.idiomatic: In response, the first corresponds to four, the second to five, the third to six.

sentences.zh: 氣氣相召，其應也必矣。

translations.literal: Qi calls to qi—the response is inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: Qi calls to qi—the response is inevitable.

sentences.zh: 卦既畫矣，故畫琴焉。

translations.literal: Once the hexagram is drawn, therefore the qin is marked.
translations.idiomatic: Once the hexagram is drawn, the qin is marked accordingly.

sentences.zh: 始以一弦泛桐，當其節則清然而號，不當其節則泯然無聲，豈人力也哉！

translations.literal: At first, touching harmonics on a single paulownia string—when it hits the division it rings clearly, when it misses the division it vanishes into silence—is this the work of human power!
translations.idiomatic: At first, touching harmonics on a single paulownia string—when it hits the proper division it rings clearly, when it misses the division it falls utterly silent—is this the work of human power alone!

sentences.zh: 且徽有十三，而居中者為一。

translations.literal: Moreover, there are thirteen stopping positions, and the one at the center counts as one.
translations.idiomatic: There are thirteen stopping positions, and the one at the center counts as the first.

sentences.zh: 自中而左泛有三焉，又右泛有三焉，其聲殺而已，弦盡則聲減。

translations.literal: From the center to the left there are three harmonics, and to the right three harmonics as well; the sound simply diminishes, and when the string is exhausted the sound fades.
translations.idiomatic: From the center, three harmonics lie to the left and three to the right; the sound simply diminishes, and when the string is exhausted the sound fades away.

sentences.zh: 及其應也，一必於四，二必於五，三必於六焉，節節相召，其應也必矣。

translations.literal: When they respond, one must be at four, two must be at five, three must be at six; division calls to division—the response is inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: In response, the first corresponds to four, the second to five, the third to six; division calls to division—the response is inevitable.

sentences.zh: 《易》之書也，偶三為六，三才之配具焉，萬物由之而出。

translations.literal: The book of the Changes pairs three to make six; the pairing of the Three Powers is complete, and the myriad things emerge from it.
translations.idiomatic: The book of the Changes pairs three to make six; the pairing of the Three Powers is complete therein, and the myriad things emerge from it.

sentences.zh: 雖曰六畫，及其數也，止三而已矣。

translations.literal: Although it is called six lines, as to its number, it stops at three alone.
translations.idiomatic: Although it is called six lines, in number it amounts to three alone.

sentences.zh: 琴之畫也，偶六而根於一，一鍾者，道之所生也。

translations.literal: The markings of the qin pair six yet are rooted in one; the one bell-tone is what the Way generates.
translations.idiomatic: The markings of the qin pair six yet are rooted in one; the single bell-tone is what the Way generates.

sentences.zh: 在數為一，在律為黃，在音為宮，在木為根，在四體為心，眾徽由之而生。

translations.literal: In number it is one, in pitch it is yellow bell, in tone it is gong, in wood it is root, in the four limbs it is heart—from it all stopping positions are generated.
translations.idiomatic: In number it is one, in pitch it is yellow bell, in tone it is gong, in wood it is root, in the four limbs it is the heart—from it all stopping positions are generated.

sentences.zh: 雖曰十三，及其節也，止三而已矣。

translations.literal: Although it is called thirteen, as to its divisions, it stops at three alone.
translations.idiomatic: Although it is called thirteen, in divisions it amounts to three alone.

sentences.zh: 卦之德方，經也；

translations.literal: The virtue of the hexagram is square—the warp;
translations.idiomatic: The virtue of the hexagram is square—it is the warp;

sentences.zh: 蓍之德圓，緯也；

translations.literal: the virtue of the yarrow stalks is round—the woof;
translations.idiomatic: the virtue of the yarrow stalks is round—it is the woof;

sentences.zh: 故萬物不能逃其象。

translations.literal: Therefore the myriad things cannot escape its images.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the myriad things cannot escape its images.

sentences.zh: 徽三其節，經也；

translations.literal: Three stopping positions triple the divisions—the warp;
translations.idiomatic: Three stopping positions triple the divisions—they are the warp;

sentences.zh: 弦五其音，緯也；

translations.literal: five strings multiply the tones—the woof;
translations.idiomatic: five strings multiply the tones—they are the woof;

sentences.zh: 故眾音不能勝其文。

translations.literal: Therefore the multitude of tones cannot surpass its pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the multitude of tones cannot surpass its pattern.

sentences.zh: 先儒謂八音以絲為君，絲以琴為君。

translations.literal: Former scholars said that among the eight sounds, silk is sovereign, and among silk the qin is sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Former scholars held that among the eight sounds silk is sovereign, and among silk the qin is sovereign.

sentences.zh: 愚謂琴以中徽為君，盡矣。

translations.literal: I hold that in the qin the center stopping position is sovereign—this is complete.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that in the qin the center stopping position is sovereign—and that is the whole of it.

sentences.zh: 夫徽十三者，蓋盡昭昭可聞者也。

translations.literal: The thirteen stopping positions are all that can be clearly heard.
translations.idiomatic: The thirteen stopping positions encompass all that can be clearly heard.

sentences.zh: 苟盡弦而考之，乃總有二十三徽焉，是一氣也。

translations.literal: If one tests every string, there are in total twenty-three stopping positions—it is one qi.
translations.idiomatic: If one tests every string thoroughly, there are twenty-three stopping positions in all—it is a single qi.

sentences.zh: 丈弦具之，尺弦亦具之，豈有長短大小之限哉！

translations.literal: The ten-foot string possesses them, the one-foot string also possesses them—how could there be limits of long and short, large and small!
translations.idiomatic: The ten-foot string possesses them, and the one-foot string does as well—what limit of long or short, large or small could there be!

sentences.zh: 是則萬物本於天地，天地本於太極，太極之外以至於萬物，聖人本於道，道本於自然，自然之外以至於無為，樂本於琴，琴本於中徽，中徽之外以至於無聲。

translations.literal: Thus the myriad things are rooted in Heaven and Earth, Heaven and Earth are rooted in the Supreme Pole; beyond the Supreme Pole one reaches the myriad things. The sage is rooted in the Way, the Way is rooted in nature; beyond nature one reaches non-action. Music is rooted in the qin, the qin is rooted in the center stopping position; beyond the center stopping position one reaches silence.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the myriad things are rooted in Heaven and Earth, and Heaven and Earth in the Supreme Pole; beyond the Supreme Pole one reaches the myriad things. The sage is rooted in the Way, and the Way in nature; beyond nature one reaches non-action. Music is rooted in the qin, and the qin in the center stopping position; beyond the center stopping position one reaches silence.

sentences.zh: 是知作《易》者，考天地之象也；

translations.literal: From this one knows that he who composed the Changes examined the images of Heaven and Earth;
translations.idiomatic: From this one knows that he who composed the Changes examined the images of Heaven and Earth;

sentences.zh: 作琴者，考天地之聲也。

translations.literal: he who composed the qin examined the sounds of Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: and he who composed the qin examined the sounds of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 往者藏音而未談，來者專聲而忘理。

translations.literal: Those of old hid the tones and did not discuss them; those who came after focused on sound and forgot principle.
translations.idiomatic: Those of old hid the tones and did not discuss them; those who came after focused on sound alone and forgot principle.

sentences.zh: 《琴箋》之作也，庶乎近之。

translations.literal: The writing of Notes on the Qin was made, perhaps, to come close to the truth.
translations.idiomatic: The writing of Notes on the Qin was intended, perhaps, to come close to the truth.

sentences.zh: 苟其闕也，請俟君子。

translations.literal: If there are deficiencies, I ask that gentlemen await and supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Where it falls short, I leave it to better men to complete.

sentences.zh: 世稱其知言。

translations.literal: The world praised him for understanding these matters.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised him for understanding these matters.

sentences.zh: 七年，東郊，建壇恭謝。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, at the Eastern Suburb, an altar was built for a reverent thanksgiving sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, at the Eastern Suburb, an altar was built for a reverent thanksgiving sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 壇上設正坐奉天地，配坐奉二聖。

translations.literal: On the altar a central seat was set to honor Heaven and Earth, and paired seats to honor the Two Sages.
translations.idiomatic: On the altar a central seat was set to honor Heaven and Earth, and paired seats to honor the Two Sages.

sentences.zh: 遵度時與張復同典記注，書昊天為天皇，又增聖祖配位，坐謬誤，降為右正言，復亦責為工部郎中。

translations.literal: At that time Zundu, together with Zhang Fu, jointly managed the record-keeping; he wrote Haotian as Heavenly Sovereign and also added a paired seat for the Sacred Ancestor; for errors in the seating arrangement he was demoted to Right Rectifier of Speech, and Fu was also penalized to become Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zundu and Zhang Fu jointly managed the record-keeping. Zundu wrote Haotian as Heavenly Sovereign and also added a paired seat for the Sacred Ancestor. For errors in the seating arrangement he was demoted to Right Rectifier of Speech, and Fu was likewise penalized with appointment as Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 踰歲，並復其秩。

translations.literal: After a year, both were restored to their ranks.
translations.idiomatic: After a year, both were restored to their former ranks.

sentences.zh: 九年，仁宗以壽春郡王開府，詔宰相擇耆德方正有學術之士，咸曰遵度力學，有士行，時稱長者，遂命與張士遜並為王友。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Emperor Renzong because the Prince of Shouchun Commandery opened a princely establishment, an edict ordered the chief councillors to select elders of virtue, integrity, and scholarly attainment; all said Zundu studied diligently, had the conduct of a scholar, and was at the time called a man of mature years; therefore he was ordered together with Zhang Shixun to serve as Friends of the Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when the Prince of Shouchun Commandery opened his princely establishment, the chief councillors were ordered to select elders of virtue, integrity, and scholarly attainment. All agreed that Zundu was diligent in study, possessed the conduct of a scholar, and was widely regarded as a man of mature years. He was therefore appointed together with Zhang Shixun as Friend of the Prince.

sentences.zh: 改戶部員外郎，賜服金紫，又賚襲衣、犀帶、緡錢。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, granted gold-purple robes, and also bestowed court robes, a rhinoceros-horn belt, and cash.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, granted gold-purple robes, and also bestowed court robes, a rhinoceros-horn belt, and cash.

sentences.zh: 上作七言詩寵之。

translations.literal: The emperor composed a seven-character poem to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor composed a seven-character poem in his honor.

sentences.zh: 因謂左右曰：「翊善、記室，皆府屬也，故王皆受拜，今賓友之禮，當令答拜。」

translations.literal: Thereupon he said to those around him: "Tutor and Record-keeper are both staff of the princely establishment, so the prince always received their bows. Now with the rites for Guest and Friend, he should be made to return the bow."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he said to those around him: "The Tutor and Record-keeper are both staff of the princely establishment, so the prince always received their bows. But with the rites for Guest and Friend, the prince should now return the bow."

sentences.zh: 府中文翰皆遵度所作。

translations.literal: All literary documents of the establishment were composed by Zundu.
translations.idiomatic: All literary documents of the establishment were composed by Zundu.

sentences.zh: 王讀《孝經》徹章，復以禦詩賜之。

translations.literal: When the prince finished reading the final chapter of the Classic of Filial Piety, he again bestowed an imperial poem upon him.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince finished reading the final chapter of the Classic of Filial Piety, the emperor again bestowed an imperial poem upon him.

sentences.zh: 國史成，拜吏部員外郎，升邸進封，改禮部郎中，充諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When the National History was completed, he was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel; when the princely residence was advanced in rank, he was changed to Director in the Ministry of Rites and appointed Consulting Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the National History was completed, he was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel. When the princely residence was advanced in rank, he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites and appointed Consulting Staff Officer.

sentences.zh: 儲宮建，又加吏部兼左諭德。

translations.literal: When the Heir Apparent's establishment was created, he was further made Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel and concurrently Left Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Heir Apparent's establishment was created, he was further made Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel and concurrently Left Mentor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，命使契丹，判司農寺。

translations.literal: Before long, he was ordered as envoy to the Khitan and served as vice director of the Directorate of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, he was sent as envoy to the Khitan and appointed vice director of the Directorate of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 遵度性寡合，喜讀《易》，嘗云：「意有疑，則彈琴辨其數，筮《易》觀其象，無不究也。」

translations.literal: Zundu by nature was sparing in company, fond of reading the Changes, and once said: "When my mind has doubt, I play the qin to discern the number, and divined the Changes to observe the image—there was nothing I did not investigate."
translations.idiomatic: Zundu was by nature reserved and sparing in company, fond of reading the Changes. He once said: "When my mind harbored doubt, I would play the qin to discern the number and consult the Changes to observe the image—there was nothing I did not investigate."

sentences.zh: 天禧四年八月卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Tianxi he died at the age of sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Tianxi he died at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 其子拜官者二人。

translations.literal: Two of his sons were granted office.
translations.idiomatic: Two of his sons were granted official posts.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，特詔贈工部侍郎，又授其二孫官，有集二十卷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, a special edict posthumously appointed him Vice Director in the Ministry of Works, and also granted office to two of his grandsons; he left a collected works in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, a special edict posthumously appointed him Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and granted office to two of his grandsons. He left collected works in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 陳越，字損之，開封尉氏人。

translations.literal: Chen Yue, courtesy name Sunzhi, was a native of Weishi in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yue, courtesy name Sunzhi, was a native of Weishi in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 祖守危，興道令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shouwei was magistrate of Xingdao.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shouwei served as magistrate of Xingdao.

sentences.zh: 父夏，虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: His father Xia was Vice Director in the Directorate of Forestry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xia served as Vice Director in the Directorate of Forestry.

sentences.zh: 越少好學，尤精歷代史。

translations.literal: Yue from youth was fond of learning and especially skilled in dynastic history.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yue was fond of learning and especially skilled in dynastic history.

sentences.zh: 善屬文，辭氣俊拔。

translations.literal: He was skilled at composing prose; his diction was lofty and forceful.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at composing prose, and his diction was lofty and forceful.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，詔舉賢良，刑部侍郎郭贄薦之，策入第四等，解褐將作監丞、通判舒州，徙知端州，又徙袁州。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era, an edict summoned men of talent and virtue; Vice Minister of Justice Guo Zi recommended him; his examination essay placed in the fourth rank; he entered service as Assistant Director in the Directorate of Public Works and transit intendant of Shuzhou, was transferred to be prefect of Duan Prefecture, and again transferred to Yuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping era, an edict summoned men of talent and virtue, and Vice Minister of Justice Guo Zi recommended him. His examination essay placed in the fourth rank. He entered service as Assistant Director in the Directorate of Public Works and transit intendant of Shuzhou, was transferred to be prefect of Duan Prefecture, and then to Yuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾召還，遷著作佐郎、直史館，掌鼓司登聞院。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned back, moved to Assistant Editor in the Palace Library and compiler attached to the History Office, and managed the Drum Office and Petition Court.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to court, promoted to Assistant Editor in the Palace Library and compiler attached to the History Office, and put in charge of the Drum Office and Petition Court.

sentences.zh: 預修《冊府元龜》，與陳從易、劉筠尤為勤職。

translations.literal: He participated in compiling the Prime Tortoise of the Archive of Books, and with Chen Congyi and Liu Yun was especially diligent in duty.
translations.idiomatic: He participated in compiling the Prime Tortoise of the Archive of Books, and with Chen Congyi and Liu Yun was especially diligent in his duties.

sentences.zh: 真宗以其奉薄，並命月增錢五千。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong because their salaries were meager ordered their monthly pay increased by five thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Because their salaries were meager, Emperor Zhenzong ordered their monthly pay increased by five thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 車駕朝陵，掌留司名表，時稱為工。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went to pay respects at the imperial tombs, he managed the memorials of the capital office in the emperor's absence; at the time he was praised for his skill.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to pay respects at the imperial tombs, Yue managed the memorials of the capital office in the emperor's absence and was praised at the time for his skill.

sentences.zh: 自是兩府箋奏多命草之，勳貴家以銘誌為請者甚眾。

translations.literal: From then on the Two Departments' memorials and reports were often ordered drafted by him, and many families of meritorious nobles requested epitaphs and inscriptions from him.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Two Departments' memorials and reports were often assigned to him for drafting, and many families of meritorious nobles requested epitaphs and inscriptions from him.

sentences.zh: 遷太常丞、群牧判官。

translations.literal: He was moved to Assistant Director in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and judge of the Pasturage Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Assistant Director in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and judge of the Pasturage Commission.

sentences.zh: 祀汾陰，擢為左正言。

translations.literal: At the sacrifice at Fenyin, he was promoted to Left Rectifier of Speech.
translations.idiomatic: At the sacrifice at Fenyin, he was promoted to Left Rectifier of Speech.

sentences.zh: 越耿概任氣，喜箴切朋友，放曠杯酒間，家徒壁立，不以屑意。

translations.literal: Yue was high-minded and free-spirited, fond of admonishing friends frankly, unrestrained over wine, his household bare as walls—he did not regard it with concern.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was high-minded and free-spirited, fond of admonishing friends frankly. Unrestrained over wine, he lived in a house bare as its walls and gave it no heed.

sentences.zh: 然嗜酒過差，每食必先引數升，罕有醒日，亦用是遘疾。

translations.literal: Yet he was excessively fond of wine; before every meal he always drank several sheng first, rarely had a sober day, and for this reason also fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he drank to excess; before every meal he would down several sheng of wine, rarely enjoyed a sober day, and for this reason also fell ill.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符五年卒，年四十。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died at the age of forty.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died at the age of forty.

sentences.zh: 無子，母老，人皆傷之。

translations.literal: He had no sons, and his mother was old; everyone grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: He left no sons, and his mother was old; everyone grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 越兄咸，嘗舉進士未第，楊億、杜鎬、陳彭年列奏為言，真宗憫之。

translations.literal: Yue's elder brother Xian had once taken the jinshi examination without passing; Yang Yi, Du Hao, and Chen Pengnian jointly memorialized on his behalf, and Emperor Zhenzong took pity on him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's elder brother Xian had once taken the jinshi examination without passing. Yang Yi, Du Hao, and Chen Pengnian jointly memorialized on his behalf, and Emperor Zhenzong took pity on him.

sentences.zh: 及《冊府元龜》奏禦，特賜咸同《三傳》出身。

translations.literal: When the Prime Tortoise of the Archive of Books was presented to the throne, Xian was specially granted the same standing as a graduate of the Three Commentaries.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prime Tortoise of the Archive of Books was presented to the throne, Xian was specially granted the same standing as a graduate of the Three Commentaries.

sentences.zh: 故事，中書章表皆舍人為之，東封後，朝廷多慶禮，舍人或以他務所嬰，乃擇館閣官，得盛度、路振、劉筠、夏竦、宋綬洎越分撰表奏，宰相嘗以名聞，其後皆相次掌外製，唯越不及登擢，時論惜之。

translations.literal: By precedent, all memorials and reports of the Secretariat were drafted by drafting academicians; after the Eastern Ascension Sacrifice, the court had many celebratory rites, and drafting academicians were sometimes occupied with other duties, so officials of the Hall and Pavilion were selected—Sheng Du, Lu Zhen, Liu Yun, Xia Song, Song Shou, and Yue among them—to divide the drafting of memorials and reports. The chief councillors once submitted their names to the throne; afterward all were in succession put in charge of external drafting, but Yue alone did not attain promotion, and opinion at the time regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, all memorials and reports of the Secretariat were drafted by drafting academicians. After the Eastern Ascension Sacrifice the court held many celebratory rites, and when drafting academicians were occupied with other duties, officials of the Hall and Pavilion were selected—Sheng Du, Lu Zhen, Liu Yun, Xia Song, Song Shou, and Yue among them—to divide the drafting of memorials and reports. The chief councillors once submitted their names to the throne, and afterward all were in succession put in charge of external drafting, but Yue alone never attained promotion—a loss widely regretted at the time.
